concepts.name: AddConstMap
concepts.docstring:
A bundled map f : G → H such that f (x + a) = f x + b for all x,
denoted as f : G →+c[a, b] H.
One can think about f as a lift to G of a map between two AddCircles.

concepts.name: AddConstMap.«term_→+c[_,_]_»
concepts.docstring:
A bundled map f : G → H such that f (x + a) = f x + b for all x,
denoted as f : G →+c[a, b] H.
One can think about f as a lift to G of a map between two AddCircles.

concepts.name: AddConstMapClass
concepts.docstring:
Typeclass for maps satisfying f (x + a) = f x + b.
Note that a and b are outParams,
so one should not add instances like
[AddConstMapClass F G H a b] : AddConstMapClass F G H (-a) (-b).

concepts.name: AddConstMap.id
concepts.docstring: The identity map as G →+c[a, a] G.

concepts.name: AddConstMap.comp
concepts.docstring: Composition of two AddConstMaps.

concepts.name: AddConstMap.replaceConsts
concepts.docstring: Change constants a and b in (f : G →+c[a, b] H) to improve definitional equalities.

concepts.name: AddConstMap.toEnd
concepts.type_signature: AddConstMap G G a a →* Function.End G
concepts.docstring: Coercion to functions as a monoid homomorphism to Function.End G.

concepts.name: AddConstMap.smul
concepts.docstring: Pointwise scalar multiplication of f : G →+c[a, b] H as a map G →+c[a, c • b] H.

concepts.name: AddConstMap.addLeftHom
concepts.type_signature: Multiplicative G →* AddConstMap G G a a
concepts.docstring:
The map that sends c to a translation by c
as a monoid homomorphism from Multiplicative G to G →+c[a, a] G.

concepts.name: AddConstMap.conjNeg
concepts.type_signature: AddConstMap G H a b ≃ AddConstMap G H a b
concepts.docstring: If f : G → H is an AddConstMap, then so is fun x ↦ -f (-x).

concepts.name: AddConstMap.mkFract
concepts.docstring: A map f : R →+c[1, a] G is defined by its values on Set.Ico 0 1.

concepts.name: AddConstEquiv
concepts.docstring:
An equivalence between G and H conjugating (· + a) to (· + b),
denoted as G ≃+c[a, b] H.

concepts.name: AddConstMap.«term_≃+c[_,_]_»
concepts.docstring:
An equivalence between G and H conjugating (· + a) to (· + b),
denoted as G ≃+c[a, b] H.

concepts.name: AddConstEquiv.symm
concepts.docstring: Inverse map of an AddConstEquiv, as an AddConstEquiv.

concepts.name: AddConstEquiv.Simps.symm_apply
concepts.docstring: A custom projection for simps.

concepts.name: AddConstEquiv.refl
concepts.docstring: The identity map as an AddConstEquiv.

concepts.name: AddConstEquiv.trans
concepts.docstring: Composition of AddConstEquivs, as an AddConstEquiv.

concepts.name: AddConstEquiv.toPerm
concepts.type_signature: AddConstEquiv G G a a →* Equiv.Perm G
concepts.docstring: Projection from G ≃+c[a, a] G to permutations G ≃ G, as a monoid homomorphism.

concepts.name: AddConstEquiv.toAddConstMapHom
concepts.type_signature: AddConstEquiv G G a a →* AddConstMap G G a a
concepts.docstring: Projection from G ≃+c[a, a] G to G →+c[a, a] G, as a monoid homomorphism.

concepts.name: AddConstEquiv.equivUnits
concepts.type_signature: AddConstEquiv G G a a ≃* (AddConstMap G G a a)ˣ
concepts.docstring: Group equivalence between G ≃+c[a, a] G and the units of G →+c[a, a] G.

concepts.name: Equiv.constVAddHom
concepts.docstring: Equiv.constVAdd as a homomorphism from Multiplicative G to Equiv.perm P

concepts.name: Function.Injective.addTorsor
concepts.docstring: Pullback of an add torsor along an injective map.

concepts.name: Function.Surjective.addTorsor
concepts.docstring: Pushforward of an add torsor along a surjective map.

concepts.name: AddTorsor
concepts.docstring:
An AddTorsor G P gives a structure to the nonempty type P,
acted on by an AddGroup G with a transitive and free action given
by the +ᵥ operation and a corresponding subtraction given by the
-ᵥ operation. In the case of a vector space, it is an affine
space.

concepts.name: Equiv.vaddConst
concepts.docstring: v ↦ v +ᵥ p as an equivalence.

concepts.name: Equiv.constVSub
concepts.docstring: p' ↦ p -ᵥ p' as an equivalence.

concepts.name: Equiv.constVAdd
concepts.docstring: The permutation given by p ↦ v +ᵥ p.

concepts.name: Equiv.pointReflection
concepts.docstring: Point reflection in x as a permutation.

concepts.name: IsAffineAddMonoid
concepts.docstring: An affine monoid is a finitely generated cancellative torsion-free commutative monoid.

concepts.name: IsAffineMonoid
concepts.docstring: An affine monoid is a finitely generated cancellative torsion-free commutative monoid.

concepts.name: AffineAddMonoid.dim
concepts.docstring: The dimension of an affine monoid M, namely the minimum n for which M embeds into ℤⁿ.

concepts.name: AffineAddMonoid.embedding
concepts.docstring: An arbitrary embedding of an affine monoid M into ℤ ^ dim M.

concepts.name: ULift.algebra'
concepts.docstring:
If A is an R-algebra, it is also a ULift R-algebra. In particular, Ulift A is a
ULift R algebra. This is not an instance, because it causes a non-reducible diamond in the case
where A = Ulift R.

concepts.name: Algebra.algebraMapSubmonoid
concepts.docstring:
Explicit characterization of the submonoid map in the case of an algebra.
S is made explicit to help with type inference

concepts.name: Algebra.semiringToRing
concepts.docstring:
A Semiring that is an Algebra over a commutative ring carries a natural Ring structure.
See note [reducible non-instances].

concepts.name: RingHom.commSemiringToCommRing
concepts.docstring: The CommRing structure on a CommSemiring induced by a ring morphism from a CommRing.

concepts.name: Invertible.algebraMapOfInvertibleAlgebraMap
concepts.docstring:
If there is a linear map f : A →ₗ[R] B that preserves 1, then algebraMap R B r is
invertible when algebraMap R A r is.

concepts.name: LinearMap.extendScalarsOfSurjectiveEquiv
concepts.docstring: If R →+* S is surjective, then S-linear maps between modules are exactly R-linear maps.

concepts.name: LinearMap.extendScalarsOfSurjective
concepts.docstring: If R →+* S is surjective, then R-linear maps are also S-linear.

concepts.name: LinearEquiv.extendScalarsOfSurjective
concepts.docstring: If R →+* S is surjective, then R-linear isomorphisms are also S-linear.

concepts.name: LinearMap.mul
concepts.docstring:
The multiplication in a non-unital non-associative algebra is a bilinear map.
A weaker version of this for semirings exists as AddMonoidHom.mul.

concepts.name: LinearMap.mul'
concepts.docstring: The multiplication map on a non-unital algebra, as an R-linear map from A ⊗[R] A to A.

concepts.name: RingTheory.LinearMap.termμ
concepts.docstring: The multiplication map on a non-unital algebra, as an R-linear map from A ⊗[R] A to A.

concepts.name: RingTheory.LinearMap.«termμ[_]»
concepts.docstring: The multiplication map on a non-unital algebra, as an R-linear map from A ⊗[R] A to A.

concepts.name: NonUnitalAlgHom.lmul
concepts.docstring:
The multiplication in a non-unital algebra is a bilinear map.
A weaker version of this for non-unital non-associative algebras exists as LinearMap.mul.

concepts.name: Algebra.lmul
concepts.docstring:
The multiplication in an algebra is an algebra homomorphism into the endomorphisms on
the algebra.
A weaker version of this for non-unital algebras exists as NonUnitalAlgHom.lmul.

concepts.name: LinearMap.mul''
concepts.docstring: The multiplication map on an R-algebra, as an A-linear map from A ⊗[R] A to A.

concepts.name: Algebra
concepts.docstring:
An associative unital R-algebra is a semiring A equipped with a map into its center R → A.
See the implementation notes in this file for discussion of the details of this definition.

concepts.name: Algebra.cast
concepts.docstring: Coercion from a commutative semiring to an algebra over this semiring.

concepts.name: RingHom.toAlgebra'
concepts.docstring:
Creating an algebra from a morphism to the center of a semiring.
See note [reducible non-instances].
Warning: In general this should not be used if S already has a SMul R S
instance, since this creates another SMul R S instance from the supplied RingHom and
this will likely create a diamond.

concepts.name: RingHom.toAlgebra
concepts.docstring:
Creating an algebra from a morphism to a commutative semiring.
See note [reducible non-instances].
Warning: In general this should not be used if S already has a SMul R S
instance, since this creates another SMul R S instance from the supplied RingHom and
this will likely create a diamond.

concepts.name: Algebra.ofModule'
concepts.docstring:
Let R be a commutative semiring, let A be a semiring with a Module R structure.
If (r • 1) * x = x * (r • 1) = r • x for all r : R and x : A, then A is an Algebra
over R.
See note [reducible non-instances].

concepts.name: Algebra.ofModule
concepts.docstring:
Let R be a commutative semiring, let A be a semiring with a Module R structure.
If (r • x) * y = x * (r • y) = r • (x * y) for all r : R and x y : A, then A
is an Algebra over R.
See note [reducible non-instances].

concepts.name: Algebra.compHom
concepts.docstring:
Compose an Algebra with a RingHom, with action f s • m.
This is the algebra version of Module.compHom.

concepts.name: Algebra.linearMap
concepts.docstring:
The canonical ring homomorphism algebraMap R A : R →+* A for any R-algebra A,
packaged as an R-linear map.

concepts.name: RingTheory.LinearMap.termη
concepts.docstring:
The canonical ring homomorphism algebraMap R A : R →+* A for any R-algebra A,
packaged as an R-linear map.

concepts.name: RingTheory.LinearMap.«termη[_]»
concepts.docstring:
The canonical ring homomorphism algebraMap R A : R →+* A for any R-algebra A,
packaged as an R-linear map.

concepts.name: Algebra.IsEpi
concepts.docstring: A commutative R-algebra A is epi, if the multiplication map A ⊗[R] A → A is injective.

concepts.name: TensorProduct.lid'
concepts.docstring: A heterogeneous variant of TensorProduct.lid when R → A is epi.

concepts.name: AlgEquiv
concepts.docstring:
An equivalence of algebras (denoted as A ≃ₐ[R] B)
is an equivalence of rings commuting with the actions of scalars.

concepts.name: «term_≃ₐ[_]_»
concepts.docstring:
An equivalence of algebras (denoted as A ≃ₐ[R] B)
is an equivalence of rings commuting with the actions of scalars.

concepts.name: AlgEquivClass
concepts.docstring:
AlgEquivClass F R A B states that F is a type of algebra structure preserving
equivalences. You should extend this class when you extend AlgEquiv.

concepts.name: AlgEquivClass.toAlgEquiv
concepts.docstring:
Turn an element of a type F satisfying AlgEquivClass F R A B into an actual AlgEquiv.
This is declared as the default coercion from F to A ≃ₐ[R] B.

concepts.name: AlgEquiv.toLinearEquiv
concepts.docstring: Forgetting the multiplicative structures, an equivalence of algebras is a linear equivalence.

concepts.name: AlgEquiv.toAlgHom
concepts.docstring:
Interpret an algebra equivalence as an algebra homomorphism.
This definition is included for symmetry with the other to*Hom projections.
The simp normal form is to use the coercion of the AlgHomClass.coeTC instance.

concepts.name: AlgEquiv.refl
concepts.docstring: Algebra equivalences are reflexive.

concepts.name: AlgEquiv.symm
concepts.docstring: Algebra equivalences are symmetric.

concepts.name: AlgEquiv.Simps.apply
concepts.docstring: See Note [custom simps projection]

concepts.name: AlgEquiv.Simps.toEquiv
concepts.docstring: See Note [custom simps projection]

concepts.name: AlgEquiv.Simps.symm_apply
concepts.docstring: See Note [custom simps projection]

concepts.name: AlgEquiv.trans
concepts.docstring: Algebra equivalences are transitive.

concepts.name: AlgEquiv.cast
concepts.docstring:
Equiv.cast (congrArg _ h) as an algebra equiv.
Note that unlike Equiv.cast, this takes an equality of indices rather than an equality of types,
to avoid having to deal with an equality of the algebraic structure itself.

concepts.name: AlgEquiv.arrowCongr
concepts.docstring:
If A₁ is equivalent to A₁' and A₂ is equivalent to A₂', then the type of maps
A₁ →ₐ[R] A₂ is equivalent to the type of maps A₁' →ₐ[R] A₂'.

concepts.name: AlgEquiv.equivCongr
concepts.docstring:
If A₁ is equivalent to A₂ and A₁' is equivalent to A₂', then the type of maps
A₁ ≃ₐ[R] A₁' is equivalent to the type of maps A₂ ≃ₐ[R] A₂'.
This is the AlgEquiv version of AlgEquiv.arrowCongr.

concepts.name: AlgEquiv.ofAlgHom
concepts.docstring: If an algebra morphism has an inverse, it is an algebra isomorphism.

concepts.name: AlgEquiv.toLinearMap
concepts.docstring: Interpret an algebra equivalence as a linear map.

concepts.name: AlgEquiv.ofBijective
concepts.docstring: Promotes a bijective algebra homomorphism to an algebra equivalence.

concepts.name: AlgEquiv.ofLinearEquiv
concepts.docstring:
Upgrade a linear equivalence to an algebra equivalence,
given that it distributes over multiplication and the identity

concepts.name: AlgEquiv.ofLinearEquiv_symm.aux
concepts.docstring: Auxiliary definition to avoid looping in dsimp with AlgEquiv.ofLinearEquiv_symm.

concepts.name: AlgEquiv.ofRingEquiv
concepts.docstring: Promotes a linear RingEquiv to an AlgEquiv.

concepts.name: AlgEquiv.autCongr
concepts.docstring:
An algebra isomorphism induces a group isomorphism between automorphism groups.
This is a more bundled version of AlgEquiv.equivCongr.

concepts.name: AlgEquiv.toAlgHomHom
concepts.docstring: AlgEquiv.toAlgHom as a MonoidHom.

concepts.name: AlgEquiv.toLinearMapHom
concepts.docstring: AlgEquiv.toLinearMap as a MonoidHom.

concepts.name: AlgEquiv.algHomUnitsEquiv
concepts.docstring:
The units group of S →ₐ[R] S is S ≃ₐ[R] S.
See LinearMap.GeneralLinearGroup.generalLinearEquiv for the linear map version.

concepts.name: MulSemiringAction.toAlgEquiv
concepts.docstring:
Each element of the group defines an algebra equivalence.
This is a stronger version of MulSemiringAction.toRingEquiv and
DistribMulAction.toLinearEquiv.

concepts.name: MulSemiringAction.toAlgAut
concepts.docstring:
Each element of the group defines an algebra equivalence.
This is a stronger version of MulSemiringAction.toRingAut and
DistribMulAction.toModuleEnd.

concepts.name: ULift.algEquiv
concepts.docstring: The algebra equivalence between ULift A and A.

concepts.name: AlgHom.ulift
concepts.type_signature: ULift.{u₁, u_2} S →ₐ[ULift.{u₂, u_1} R] ULift.{u₃, u_3} T
concepts.docstring: ULift is functorial for algebra homomorphisms.

concepts.name: LinearEquiv.algEquivOfRing
concepts.docstring:
If an R-algebra A is isomorphic to R as R-module, then the canonical map R → A is an
equivalence of R-algebras.
Note that if e : R ≃ₗ[R] A is the linear equivalence, then this is not the same as the equivalence
of algebras provided here unless e 1 = 1.

concepts.name: LinearEquiv.conjAlgEquiv
concepts.type_signature: Module.End S M₁ ≃ₐ[R] Module.End S M₂
concepts.docstring:
A linear equivalence of two modules induces an equivalence of algebras of their
endomorphisms.

concepts.name: LinearEquiv.algConj
concepts.type_signature: Module.End S M₁ ≃ₐ[R] Module.End S M₂
concepts.docstring:
Alias of LinearEquiv.conjAlgEquiv.
A linear equivalence of two modules induces an equivalence of algebras of their
endomorphisms.

concepts.name: RingHom.toRatAlgHom
concepts.docstring:
Reinterpret a RingHom as a ℚ-algebra homomorphism. This actually yields an equivalence,
see RingHom.equivRatAlgHom.

concepts.name: RingHom.equivRatAlgHom
concepts.docstring: The equivalence between RingHom and ℚ-algebra homomorphisms.

concepts.name: AlgHom
concepts.docstring: Defining the homomorphism in the category R-Alg, denoted A →ₐ[R] B.

concepts.name: «term_→ₐ_»
concepts.docstring: Defining the homomorphism in the category R-Alg, denoted A →ₐ[R] B.

concepts.name: «term_→ₐ[_]_»
concepts.docstring: Defining the homomorphism in the category R-Alg, denoted A →ₐ[R] B.

concepts.name: AlgHomClass
concepts.docstring:
AlgHomClass F R A B asserts F is a type of bundled algebra homomorphisms
from A to B.

concepts.name: AlgHomClass.toAlgHom
concepts.docstring:
Turn an element of a type F satisfying AlgHomClass F α β into an actual
AlgHom. This is declared as the default coercion from F to α →+* β.

concepts.name: AlgHom.Simps.apply
concepts.docstring: See Note [custom simps projection]

concepts.name: AlgHom.toMonoidHom'
concepts.docstring: Turn an algebra homomorphism into the corresponding multiplicative monoid homomorphism.

concepts.name: AlgHom.toAddMonoidHom'
concepts.docstring: Turn an algebra homomorphism into the corresponding additive monoid homomorphism.

concepts.name: AlgHom.mk'
concepts.docstring: If a RingHom is R-linear, then it is an AlgHom.

concepts.name: AlgHom.id
concepts.docstring: Identity map as an AlgHom.

concepts.name: AlgHom.comp
concepts.docstring:
If φ₁ and φ₂ are R-algebra homomorphisms with the
domain of φ₁ equal to the codomain of φ₂, then
φ₁.comp φ₂ is the algebra homomorphism x ↦ φ₁ (φ₂ x).

concepts.name: AlgHom.toLinearMap
concepts.docstring: R-Alg ⥤ R-Mod

concepts.name: AlgHom.ofLinearMap
concepts.docstring: Promote a LinearMap to an AlgHom by supplying proofs about the behavior on 1 and *.

concepts.name: AlgHom.toEnd
concepts.docstring: AlgHom.toLinearMap as a MonoidHom.

concepts.name: IsScalarTower.toAlgHom
concepts.docstring:
In a tower, the canonical map from the middle element to the top element is an
algebra homomorphism over the bottom element.

concepts.name: Algebra.algHom
concepts.docstring: The algebra morphism underlying algebraMap.

concepts.name: RingHom.toNatAlgHom
concepts.docstring: Reinterpret a RingHom as an ℕ-algebra homomorphism.

concepts.name: RingHom.toIntAlgHom
concepts.docstring: Reinterpret a RingHom as a ℤ-algebra homomorphism.

concepts.name: Algebra.ofId
concepts.docstring: AlgebraMap as an AlgHom.

concepts.name: MulSemiringAction.toAlgHom
concepts.docstring:
Each element of the monoid defines an algebra homomorphism.
This is a stronger version of MulSemiringAction.toRingHom and
DistribSMul.toLinearMap.

concepts.name: NonUnitalAlgHom
concepts.docstring:
A morphism respecting addition, multiplication, and scalar multiplication
(denoted as A →ₛₙₐ[φ] B, or A →ₙₐ[R] B when φ is the identity on R).
When these arise from algebra structures, this is the same
as a not-necessarily-unital morphism of algebras.

concepts.name: «term_→ₙₐ_»
concepts.docstring:
A morphism respecting addition, multiplication, and scalar multiplication
(denoted as A →ₛₙₐ[φ] B, or A →ₙₐ[R] B when φ is the identity on R).
When these arise from algebra structures, this is the same
as a not-necessarily-unital morphism of algebras.

concepts.name: «term_→ₛₙₐ[_]_»
concepts.docstring:
A morphism respecting addition, multiplication, and scalar multiplication
(denoted as A →ₛₙₐ[φ] B, or A →ₙₐ[R] B when φ is the identity on R).
When these arise from algebra structures, this is the same
as a not-necessarily-unital morphism of algebras.

concepts.name: «term_→ₙₐ[_]_»
concepts.docstring:
A morphism respecting addition, multiplication, and scalar multiplication
(denoted as A →ₛₙₐ[φ] B, or A →ₙₐ[R] B when φ is the identity on R).
When these arise from algebra structures, this is the same
as a not-necessarily-unital morphism of algebras.

concepts.name: NonUnitalAlgSemiHomClass
concepts.docstring:
NonUnitalAlgSemiHomClass F φ A B asserts F is a type of bundled algebra homomorphisms
from A to B which are equivariant with respect to φ.

concepts.name: NonUnitalAlgHomClass
concepts.docstring:
NonUnitalAlgHomClass F R A B asserts F is a type of bundled algebra homomorphisms
from A to B which are R-linear.
This is an abbreviation to NonUnitalAlgSemiHomClass F (MonoidHom.id R) A B

concepts.name: NonUnitalAlgHomClass.toNonUnitalAlgSemiHom
concepts.docstring:
Turn an element of a type F satisfying NonUnitalAlgSemiHomClass F φ A B into an actual
NonUnitalAlgHom. This is declared as the default coercion from F to A →ₛₙₐ[φ] B.

concepts.name: NonUnitalAlgHomClass.toNonUnitalAlgHom
concepts.docstring:
Turn an element of a type F satisfying NonUnitalAlgHomClass F R A B into an actual
@[coe]
NonUnitalAlgHom. This is declared as the default coercion from F to A →ₛₙₐ[R] B.

concepts.name: NonUnitalAlgHom.Simps.apply
concepts.docstring: See Note [custom simps projection]

concepts.name: NonUnitalAlgHom.id
concepts.docstring: The identity map as a NonUnitalAlgHom.

concepts.name: NonUnitalAlgHom.comp
concepts.docstring: The composition of morphisms is a morphism.

concepts.name: NonUnitalAlgHom.inverse
concepts.docstring: The inverse of a bijective morphism is a morphism.

concepts.name: NonUnitalAlgHom.inverse'
concepts.docstring: The inverse of a bijective morphism is a morphism.

concepts.name: NonUnitalAlgHom.fst
concepts.docstring: The first projection of a product is a non-unital algebra homomorphism.

concepts.name: NonUnitalAlgHom.snd
concepts.docstring: The second projection of a product is a non-unital algebra homomorphism.

concepts.name: NonUnitalAlgHom.prod
concepts.docstring: The prod of two morphisms is a morphism.

concepts.name: NonUnitalAlgHom.prodEquiv
concepts.docstring:
Taking the product of two maps with the same domain is equivalent to taking the product of
their codomains.

concepts.name: NonUnitalAlgHom.inl
concepts.docstring: The left injection into a product is a non-unital algebra homomorphism.

concepts.name: NonUnitalAlgHom.inr
concepts.docstring: The right injection into a product is a non-unital algebra homomorphism.

concepts.name: AlgHom.toNonUnitalAlgHom
concepts.docstring: A unital morphism of algebras is a NonUnitalAlgHom.

concepts.name: NonUnitalAlgHom.restrictScalars
concepts.docstring:
If a monoid R acts on another monoid S, then a non-unital algebra homomorphism
over S can be viewed as a non-unital algebra homomorphism over R.

concepts.name: NonUnitalSubalgebraClass.subtype
concepts.docstring: Embedding of a non-unital subalgebra into the non-unital algebra.

concepts.name: NonUnitalSubalgebra
concepts.docstring: A non-unital subalgebra is a sub(semi)ring that is also a submodule.

concepts.name: NonUnitalSubalgebra.ofClass
concepts.docstring:
The actual NonUnitalSubalgebra obtained from an element of a type satisfying
NonUnitalSubsemiringClass and SMulMemClass.

concepts.name: NonUnitalSubalgebra.copy
concepts.docstring:
Copy of a non-unital subalgebra with a new carrier equal to the old one.
Useful to fix definitional equalities.

concepts.name: NonUnitalSubalgebra.toNonUnitalSubring
concepts.docstring: A non-unital subalgebra over a ring is also a Subring.

concepts.name: NonUnitalSubalgebra.toSubmodule'
concepts.type_signature: NonUnitalSubalgebra R A ↪o Submodule R A
concepts.docstring: The forgetful map from NonUnitalSubalgebra to Submodule as an OrderEmbedding

concepts.name: NonUnitalSubalgebra.toNonUnitalSubsemiring'
concepts.docstring:
The forgetful map from NonUnitalSubalgebra to NonUnitalSubsemiring as an
OrderEmbedding

concepts.name: NonUnitalSubalgebra.toNonUnitalSubring'
concepts.docstring:
The forgetful map from NonUnitalSubalgebra to NonUnitalSubsemiring as an
OrderEmbedding

concepts.name: NonUnitalSubalgebra.toSubmoduleEquiv
concepts.docstring:
Linear equivalence between S : Submodule R A and S. Though these types are equal,
we define it as a LinearEquiv to avoid type equalities.

concepts.name: NonUnitalSubalgebra.map
concepts.docstring: Transport a non-unital subalgebra via an algebra homomorphism.

concepts.name: NonUnitalSubalgebra.comap
concepts.docstring: Preimage of a non-unital subalgebra under an algebra homomorphism.

concepts.name: Submodule.toNonUnitalSubalgebra
concepts.docstring: A submodule closed under multiplication is a non-unital subalgebra.

concepts.name: NonUnitalAlgHom.range
concepts.docstring: Range of an NonUnitalAlgHom as a non-unital subalgebra.

concepts.name: NonUnitalAlgHom.codRestrict
concepts.docstring: Restrict the codomain of a non-unital algebra homomorphism.

concepts.name: NonUnitalAlgHom.rangeRestrict
concepts.docstring:
Restrict the codomain of an NonUnitalAlgHom f to f.range.
This is the bundled version of Set.rangeFactorization.

concepts.name: NonUnitalAlgHom.equalizer
concepts.docstring: The equalizer of two non-unital R-algebra homomorphisms

concepts.name: NonUnitalAlgebra.adjoin
concepts.docstring: The minimal non-unital subalgebra that includes s.

concepts.name: NonUnitalAlgebra.gi
concepts.docstring: Galois insertion between adjoin and SetLike.coe.

concepts.name: NonUnitalAlgebra.toTop
concepts.docstring: NonUnitalAlgHom to ⊤ : NonUnitalSubalgebra R A.

concepts.name: NonUnitalSubalgebra.prod
concepts.docstring: The product of two non-unital subalgebras is a non-unital subalgebra.

concepts.name: NonUnitalSubalgebra.inclusion
concepts.docstring:
The map S → T when S is a non-unital subalgebra contained in the non-unital subalgebra T.
This is the non-unital subalgebra version of Submodule.inclusion, or Subring.inclusion

concepts.name: NonUnitalSubalgebra.iSupLift
concepts.docstring:
Define an algebra homomorphism on a directed supremum of non-unital subalgebras by defining
it on each non-unital subalgebra, and proving that it agrees on the intersection of
non-unital subalgebras.

concepts.name: NonUnitalSubalgebra.center
concepts.docstring:
The center of a non-unital algebra is the set of elements which commute with every element.
They form a non-unital subalgebra.

concepts.name: NonUnitalSubalgebra.centralizer
concepts.docstring: The centralizer of a set as a non-unital subalgebra.

concepts.name: NonUnitalAlgebra.adjoinNonUnitalCommSemiringOfComm
concepts.docstring:

semiring.
See note [reducible non-instances].

concepts.name: NonUnitalAlgebra.adjoinNonUnitalCommRingOfComm
concepts.docstring:
If all elements of s : Set A commute pairwise, then adjoin R s is a non-unital commutative
ring.
See note [reducible non-instances].

concepts.name: nonUnitalSubalgebraOfNonUnitalSubsemiring
concepts.docstring: A non-unital subsemiring is a non-unital ℕ-subalgebra.

concepts.name: nonUnitalSubalgebraOfNonUnitalSubring
concepts.docstring: A non-unital subring is a non-unital ℤ-subalgebra.

concepts.name: Submodule.hasDistribPointwiseNeg

concepts.name: Submodule.equivOpposite

submodules.

concepts.name: Submodule.span.ringHom

span is a semiring homomorphism (recall multiplication is pointwise multiplication of subsets
on either side).

concepts.name: Submodule.spanSingleton

concepts.name: Submodule.pointwiseMulSemiringAction

This is available as an instance in the Pointwise locale.
This is a stronger version of Submodule.pointwiseDistribMulAction.

concepts.name: AlgEquiv.opOp

An algebra homomorphism f : A →ₐ[R] B such that f x commutes with f y for all x, y defines
an algebra homomorphism from Aᵐᵒᵖ.

concepts.name: AlgHom.toOpposite
concepts.docstring:
An algebra homomorphism f : A →ₐ[R] B such that f x commutes with f y for all x, y defines
an algebra homomorphism to Bᵐᵒᵖ.

concepts.name: AlgHom.op
concepts.docstring:
An algebra hom A →ₐ[R] B can equivalently be viewed as an algebra hom Aᵐᵒᵖ →ₐ[R] Bᵐᵒᵖ.
This is the action of the (fully faithful) ᵐᵒᵖ-functor on morphisms.

concepts.name: AlgHom.unop

concepts.name: AlgHom.opComm
concepts.docstring: Swap the ᵐᵒᵖ on an algebra hom to the opposite side.

concepts.name: AlgEquiv.op
concepts.docstring:
An algebra iso A ≃ₐ[R] B can equivalently be viewed as an algebra iso Aᵐᵒᵖ ≃ₐ[R] Bᵐᵒᵖ.
This is the action of the (fully faithful) ᵐᵒᵖ-functor on morphisms.

concepts.name: AlgEquiv.unop
concepts.docstring: The 'unopposite' of an algebra iso Aᵐᵒᵖ ≃ₐ[R] Bᵐᵒᵖ. Inverse to AlgEquiv.op.

concepts.name: AlgEquiv.opComm
concepts.docstring: Swap the ᵐᵒᵖ on an algebra isomorphism to the opposite side.

concepts.name: AlgEquiv.moduleEndSelf
concepts.docstring:
The canonical algebra isomorphism from Aᵐᵒᵖ to Module.End A A induced by the right
multiplication.

concepts.name: AlgEquiv.moduleEndSelfOp
concepts.docstring:
The canonical algebra isomorphism from A to Module.End Aᵐᵒᵖ A induced by the left
multiplication.

concepts.name: AlgEquiv.toOpposite
concepts.docstring: A commutative algebra is isomorphic to its opposite.

concepts.name: Pi.algHom
concepts.docstring:
A family of algebra homomorphisms g i : B →ₐ[R] A i defines a ring homomorphism
Pi.algHom g : B →ₐ[R] Π i, A i given by Pi.algHom g x i = g i x.

concepts.name: Pi.evalAlgHom

Function.eval as an AlgHom. The name matches Pi.evalRingHom, Pi.evalMonoidHom,
etc.

concepts.name: Pi.constAlgHom

R-algebra homomorphism between the function spaces ι → A and ι → B, induced by an
R-algebra homomorphism f between A and B.

concepts.name: AlgEquiv.piCongrRight

concepts.name: AlgEquiv.piMulOpposite

The opposite of a direct product is isomorphic to the direct product of the opposites as

This is Equiv.piCongrLeft' as an AlgEquiv.

Transport dependent functions through an equivalence of the base space, expressed as

This is Equiv.piCongrLeft as an AlgEquiv.

concepts.name: AlgEquiv.funUnique

Taking the product of two maps with the same domain is equivalent to taking the product of

concepts.docstring:
Multiplying by the trivial algebra from the right does not change the structure.
This is the AlgEquiv version of LinearEquiv.prodUnique and RingEquiv.prodZeroRing.symm.

concepts.name: AlgEquiv.uniqueProd
concepts.docstring:
Multiplying by the trivial algebra from the left does not change the structure.
This is the AlgEquiv version of LinearEquiv.uniqueProd and RingEquiv.zeroRingProd.symm.

concepts.name: RestrictScalars
concepts.docstring:
If we put an R-algebra structure on a semiring S, we get a natural equivalence from the
category of S-modules to the category of representations of the algebra S (over R). The type
synonym RestrictScalars is essentially this equivalence.
Warning: use this type synonym judiciously! Consider an example where we want to construct an
R-linear map from M to S, given:
With the assumptions above we can't directly state our map as we have no Module R M structure, but
RestrictScalars permits it to be written as:
However, it is usually better just to add this extra structure as an argument:
The advantage of the second approach is that it defers the duty of providing the missing typeclasses
[Module R M] [IsScalarTower R S M]. If some concrete M naturally carries these (as is often
the case) then we have avoided RestrictScalars entirely. If not, we can pass
RestrictScalars R S M later on instead of M.
Note that this means we almost always want to state definitions and lemmas in the language of
IsScalarTower rather than RestrictScalars.
An example of when one might want to use RestrictScalars would be if one has a vector space
over a field of characteristic zero and wishes to make use of the ℚ-algebra structure.

concepts.name: RestrictScalars.moduleOrig
concepts.docstring: We temporarily install an action of the original ring on RestrictScalars R S M.

concepts.name: Module.restrictScalars
concepts.docstring:
When M is a module over a ring S, and S is an algebra over R, then M inherits a
module structure over R. Not an instance because S cannot be inferred.
The preferred way of setting this up is [Module R M] [Module S M] [IsScalarTower R S M].

concepts.name: RestrictScalars.lsmul
concepts.type_signature: S →ₐ[R] Module.End R (RestrictScalars R S M)
concepts.docstring:
The R-algebra homomorphism from the original coefficient algebra S to endomorphisms
of RestrictScalars R S M.

concepts.name: RestrictScalars.addEquiv
concepts.docstring: RestrictScalars.addEquiv is the additive equivalence with the original module.

concepts.name: RestrictScalars.ringEquiv
concepts.docstring: Tautological ring isomorphism RestrictScalars R S A ≃+* A.

concepts.name: Algebra.restrictScalars
concepts.docstring: R ⟶ S induces S-Alg ⥤ R-Alg. Not an instance because S cannot be inferred.

concepts.name: Shrink.algEquiv
concepts.docstring: Shrinking α to a smaller universe preserves algebra structure.

concepts.name: resolventSet
concepts.docstring:
Given a commutative ring R and an R-algebra A, the resolvent set of a : A
is the Set R consisting of those r : R for which r•1 - a is a unit of the
algebra A.

concepts.name: spectrum
concepts.docstring:
Given a commutative ring R and an R-algebra A, the spectrum of a : A
is the Set R consisting of those r : R for which r•1 - a is not a unit of the
algebra A.
The spectrum is simply the complement of the resolvent set.

concepts.name: resolvent
concepts.docstring:
Given an a : A where A is an R-algebra, the resolvent is
a map R → A which sends r : R to (algebraMap R A r - a)⁻¹ when
r ∈ resolvent R A and 0 when r ∈ spectrum R A.

concepts.name: IsUnit.subInvSMul
concepts.docstring: The unit 1 - r⁻¹ • a constructed from r • 1 - a when the latter is a unit.

concepts.name: PreQuasiregular.toPi
concepts.type_signature: PreQuasiregular ((i : ι) → κ i) ≃* ((i : ι) → PreQuasiregular (κ i))
concepts.docstring:
The equivalence between pre-quasiregular elements of an indexed product and the indexed product
of pre-quasiregular elements.

concepts.name: PreQuasiregular.toProd
concepts.type_signature: PreQuasiregular (A × B) ≃* PreQuasiregular A × PreQuasiregular B
concepts.docstring:
The equivalence between pre-quasiregular elements of a product and the product of
pre-quasiregular elements.

concepts.name: PreQuasiregular
concepts.docstring:
A type synonym for non-unital rings where an alternative monoid structure is introduced.
If R is a non-unital semiring, then PreQuasiregular R is equipped with the monoid structure
with binary operation fun x y ↦ y + x + x * y and identity 0. Elements of R which are
invertible in this monoid satisfy the predicate IsQuasiregular.

concepts.name: PreQuasiregular.equiv
concepts.docstring: The identity map between R and PreQuasiregular R.

concepts.name: Unitization.unitsFstOne
concepts.docstring: The subgroup of the units of Unitization R A whose scalar part is 1.

concepts.name: Unitization.unitsFstOne_mulEquiv_quasiregular
concepts.docstring:
If A is a non-unital R-algebra, then the subgroup of units of Unitization R A whose
scalar part is 1 : R (i.e., Unitization.unitsFstOne) is isomorphic to the group of units of
PreQuasiregular A.

concepts.name: IsQuasiregular
concepts.docstring:
In a non-unital semiring R, an element x : R satisfies IsQuasiregular if it is a unit
under the monoid operation fun x y ↦ y + x + x * y.

concepts.name: quasispectrum
concepts.docstring:
If A is a non-unital R-algebra, the R-quasispectrum of a : A consists of those r : R
such that if r is invertible (in R), then -(r⁻¹ • a) is not quasiregular.
The quasispectrum is precisely the spectrum in the unitization when R is a commutative ring.
See Unitization.quasispectrum_eq_spectrum_inr.

concepts.name: NonnegSpectrumClass
concepts.docstring:
A class for 𝕜-algebras with a partial order where the ordering is compatible with the
(quasi)spectrum.

concepts.name: QuasispectrumRestricts
concepts.docstring:
Given an element a : A of an S-algebra, where S is itself an R-algebra, we say that
the spectrum of a restricts via a function f : S → R if f is a left inverse of
algebraMap R S, and f is a right inverse of algebraMap R S on spectrum S a.
For example, when f = Complex.re (so S := ℂ and R := ℝ), SpectrumRestricts a f means that
the ℂ-spectrum of a is contained within ℝ. This arises naturally when a is selfadjoint
and A is a C⋆-algebra.
This is the property allows us to restrict a continuous functional calculus over S to a
continuous functional calculus over R.

concepts.name: SpectrumRestricts
concepts.docstring:
A (reducible) alias of QuasispectrumRestricts which enforces stronger type class assumptions
on the types involved, as it's really intended for the spectrum. The separate definition also
allows for dot notation.

concepts.name: IsStrictlyPositive
concepts.docstring:
An element of an ordered algebra is strictly positive if it is nonnegative and invertible.
NOTE: This definition will be generalized to the non-unital case in the future; do not unfold
the definition and use the API provided instead to avoid breakage when the refactor happens.

concepts.name: Subalgebra
concepts.docstring: A subalgebra is a sub(semi)ring that includes the range of algebraMap.

concepts.name: Subalgebra.ofClass
concepts.docstring:
The actual Subalgebra obtained from an element of a type satisfying SubsemiringClass and
SMulMemClass.

concepts.name: Subalgebra.copy
concepts.docstring:
Copy of a subalgebra with a new carrier equal to the old one. Useful to fix definitional
equalities.

concepts.name: Subalgebra.toNonUnitalSubalgebra
concepts.docstring: Turn a Subalgebra into a NonUnitalSubalgebra by forgetting that it contains 1.

concepts.name: Subalgebra.toAddSubmonoid
concepts.docstring: The projection from a subalgebra of A to an additive submonoid of A.

concepts.name: Subalgebra.toSubring
concepts.docstring: A subalgebra over a ring is also a Subring.

concepts.name: Subalgebra.toSubmodule
concepts.type_signature: Subalgebra R A ↪o Submodule R A
concepts.docstring: The forgetful map from Subalgebra to Submodule as an OrderEmbedding

concepts.name: Subalgebra.val
concepts.docstring: Embedding of a subalgebra into the algebra.

concepts.name: Subalgebra.toSubmoduleEquiv
concepts.docstring:
Linear equivalence between S : Submodule R A and S. Though these types are equal,
we define it as a LinearEquiv to avoid type equalities.

concepts.name: Subalgebra.map

concepts.name: Subalgebra.comap

concepts.name: SubalgebraClass.val
concepts.docstring: Embedding of a subalgebra into the algebra, as an algebra homomorphism.

concepts.name: Submodule.toSubalgebra
concepts.docstring: A submodule containing 1 and closed under multiplication is a subalgebra.

concepts.name: AlgHom.range

concepts.name: AlgHom.codRestrict
concepts.docstring: Restrict the codomain of an algebra homomorphism.

concepts.name: AlgHom.rangeRestrict

Restrict the codomain of an AlgHom f to f.range.

concepts.name: AlgEquiv.ofLeftInverse
concepts.docstring:
Restrict an algebra homomorphism with a left inverse to an algebra isomorphism to its range.

concepts.name: AlgEquiv.ofInjective
concepts.docstring: Restrict an injective algebra homomorphism to an algebra isomorphism

concepts.name: AlgEquiv.ofInjectiveField
concepts.docstring: Restrict an algebra homomorphism between fields to an algebra isomorphism

concepts.name: AlgEquiv.subalgebraMap
concepts.docstring:
Given an equivalence e : A ≃ₐ[R] B of R-algebras and a subalgebra S of A,
subalgebraMap is the induced equivalence between S and S.map e

concepts.name: Subalgebra.inclusion
concepts.docstring:
The map S → T when S is a subalgebra contained in the subalgebra T.
This is the subalgebra version of Submodule.inclusion, or Subring.inclusion

concepts.name: Subalgebra.equivOfEq
concepts.docstring:
Two subalgebras that are equal are also equivalent as algebras.
This is the Subalgebra version of LinearEquiv.ofEq and Equiv.setCongr.

concepts.name: AlgHom.subalgebraMap
concepts.docstring:
An AlgHom between two rings restricts to an AlgHom from any subalgebra of the
domain onto the image of that subalgebra.

concepts.name: Subalgebra.equivMapOfInjective
concepts.docstring: A subalgebra is isomorphic to its image under an injective AlgHom

concepts.name: Subalgebra.center
concepts.docstring:
The center of an algebra is the set of elements which commute with every element. They form a
subalgebra.

concepts.name: Subalgebra.centralizer
concepts.docstring: The centralizer of a set as a subalgebra.

concepts.name: subalgebraOfSubsemiring
concepts.docstring: A subsemiring is an ℕ-subalgebra.

concepts.name: subalgebraOfSubring
concepts.docstring: A subring is a ℤ-subalgebra.

concepts.name: AlgHom.equalizer
concepts.docstring: The equalizer of two R-algebra homomorphisms

concepts.name: NonUnitalSubalgebra.toSubalgebra
concepts.docstring: Turn a non-unital subalgebra containing 1 into a subalgebra.

concepts.name: Subalgebra.iSupLift
concepts.docstring:
Define an algebra homomorphism on a directed supremum of subalgebras by defining
it on each subalgebra, and proving that it agrees on the intersection of subalgebras.

concepts.name: Algebra.adjoin
concepts.docstring: The minimal subalgebra that includes s.

concepts.name: Algebra.gi
concepts.docstring: Galois insertion between adjoin and coe.

concepts.name: Algebra.toTop
concepts.docstring: AlgHom to ⊤ : Subalgebra R A.

concepts.name: Algebra.botEquivOfInjective
concepts.docstring: The bottom subalgebra is isomorphic to the base ring.

concepts.name: Algebra.botEquiv
concepts.docstring: The bottom subalgebra is isomorphic to the field.

concepts.name: Subalgebra.topEquiv
concepts.docstring:
The top subalgebra is isomorphic to the algebra.
This is the algebra version of Submodule.topEquiv.

concepts.name: Subalgebra.saturation
concepts.docstring:
The saturation of a subalgebra s with respect to a submonoid M is the smallest
subalgebra closed under division by s.

concepts.name: Algebra.subalgebra_adjoin
concepts.docstring: If x₁ x₂ ... xₙ : A then R[x₁,x₂,...,xₙ] is the Subalgebra R A generated by these elements.

concepts.name: Algebra.delabAdjoinNotation
concepts.docstring: Supporting function for the R[x₁,x₂,...,xₙ] adjunction notation.

concepts.name: Algebra.CoeAdjoinAux
concepts.docstring: Supporting class for coercions xₖ : R[x₁, ..., xₙ].

concepts.docstring:
Enables notation xₖ : R[x₁, ..., xₙ] instead of

concepts.name: Algebra.adjoinCommSemiringOfComm
concepts.docstring:
If all elements of s : Set A commute pairwise, then adjoin R s is a non-unital commutative
semiring.
See note [reducible non-instances].

concepts.name: Algebra.adjoinCommRingOfComm
concepts.docstring:
If all elements of s : Set A commute pairwise, then adjoin R s is a commutative
ring.

concepts.name: Subsemiring.closureEquivAdjoinNat
concepts.docstring:
The ℕ-algebra equivalence between Subsemiring.closure s and Algebra.adjoin ℕ s given

concepts.name: Subring.closureEquivAdjoinInt

concepts.name: Subalgebra.toNonUnitalSubalgebraOrderEmbedding

Given a Subalgebra S, S.matrix is the Subalgebra of square matrices m

concepts.name: Subalgebra.op

concepts.name: Subalgebra.unop
concepts.docstring: Pull a subalgebra back to a subalgebra along MulOpposite.op

concepts.name: Subalgebra.opEquiv
concepts.type_signature: Subalgebra R A ≃o Subalgebra R Aᵐᵒᵖ
concepts.docstring: A subalgebra S of A / R determines a subalgebra S.op of the opposite ring Aᵐᵒᵖ / R.

concepts.name: Subalgebra.linearEquivOp
concepts.docstring: Bijection between a subalgebra S and its opposite.

concepts.name: Subalgebra.algEquivOpMop

concepts.name: Subalgebra.mopAlgEquivOp

concepts.name: FixedPoints.subsemiring
concepts.docstring: The set of fixed points under a group action, as a subring.

concepts.name: FixedPoints.subring
concepts.docstring: The set of fixed points under a group action, as a subring.

concepts.name: FixedPoints.subalgebra
concepts.docstring: The set of fixed points under a group action, as a subalgebra.

concepts.name: Subalgebra.pi
concepts.docstring: The product of subalgebras as a subalgebra.

concepts.name: Subalgebra.pointwiseMulAction
concepts.docstring:
The action on a subalgebra corresponding to applying the action to every element.
This is available as an instance in the Pointwise locale.

concepts.name: Subalgebra.prod
concepts.docstring: The product of two subalgebras is a subalgebra.

concepts.name: Subalgebra.restrictScalars
concepts.docstring:

U as an R-subalgebra of A.

concepts.name: Subalgebra.ofRestrictScalars
concepts.docstring:

This is a special case of AlgHom.restrictScalars that can be helpful in elaboration.

concepts.name: NonUnitalSubalgebra.unitization
concepts.docstring:
The natural R-algebra homomorphism from the unitization of a non-unital subalgebra into
the algebra containing it.

concepts.name: NonUnitalSubalgebra.unitizationAlgEquiv
concepts.docstring:
If a NonUnitalSubalgebra over a field does not contain 1, then its unitization is
isomorphic to its Algebra.adjoin.

concepts.name: NonUnitalSubsemiring.unitization
concepts.docstring:
The natural ℕ-algebra homomorphism from the unitization of a non-unital subsemiring to
its Subsemiring.closure.

concepts.name: NonUnitalSubring.unitization
concepts.docstring:
The natural ℤ-algebra homomorphism from the unitization of a non-unital subring to
its Subring.closure.

concepts.name: NonUnitalStarSubalgebra.unitization
concepts.docstring:
The natural star R-algebra homomorphism from the unitization of a non-unital star subalgebra
to its StarAlgebra.adjoin.

concepts.name: NonUnitalStarSubalgebra.unitizationStarAlgEquiv
concepts.docstring:
If a NonUnitalStarSubalgebra over a field does not contain 1, then its unitization is
isomorphic to its StarAlgebra.adjoin.

concepts.name: Algebra.lsmul
concepts.docstring:
The R-algebra morphism A → End (M) corresponding to the representation of the algebra A
on the B-module M.
This is a stronger version of DistribSMul.toLinearMap, and could also have been
called Algebra.toModuleEnd.
The typeclasses correspond to the situation where the types act on each other as
where the diagram commutes, the action by R commutes with everything, and the action by A and
B on M commute.
Typically this is most useful with B = R as Algebra.lsmul R R A : A →ₐ[R] Module.End R M.
However this can be used to get the fact that left-multiplication by A is right A-linear, and
vice versa, as
respectively; though LinearMap.mulLeft and LinearMap.mulRight can also be used here.

concepts.name: AlgHom.restrictScalars
concepts.docstring: R ⟶ S induces S-Alg ⥤ R-Alg

concepts.name: AlgHom.extendScalarsOfSurjective
concepts.docstring:

A and B factors via R ⧸ I.

concepts.name: Unitization

concepts.docstring:
The coercion from a non-unital R-algebra A to its unitization Unitization R A
realized as a non-unital algebra homomorphism.

concepts.name: Unitization.inrNonUnitalStarAlgHom

The coercion from a non-unital R-algebra A to its unitization Unitization R A

reasons.

concepts.name: Unitization.lift
concepts.docstring:
Non-unital algebra homomorphisms from A into a unital R-algebra C lift uniquely to
Unitization R A →ₐ[R] C. This is the universal property of the unitization.

concepts.name: Unitization.starLift
concepts.docstring:
Non-unital star algebra homomorphisms from A into a unital star R-algebra C lift uniquely
to Unitization R A →⋆ₐ[R] C. This is the universal property of the unitization.

concepts.name: Unitization.starMap
concepts.type_signature: Unitization R A →⋆ₐ[R] Unitization R B
concepts.docstring:
The functorial map on morphisms between the category of non-unital C⋆-algebras with non-unital
star homomorphisms and unital C⋆-algebras with unital star homomorphisms.
This sends φ : A →⋆ₙₐ[R] B to a map Unitization R A →⋆ₐ[R] Unitization R B given by the formula
(r, a) ↦ (r, φ a) (or perhaps more precisely,
algebraMap R _ r + ↑a ↦ algebraMap R _ r + ↑(φ a)).

An Azumaya algebra is a finitely generated, projective and faithful R-algebra where

by sending f to ∑ᵢₗₛₜ f(Eₛₜ)ᵢₗ • Eᵢₛ⊗Eₜₗ.

concepts.name: finsum

Sum of f x as x ranges over the elements of the support of f, if it's finite. Zero
otherwise.

concepts.name: finprod
concepts.docstring:
Product of f x as x ranges over the elements of the multiplicative support of f, if it's
finite. One otherwise.

concepts.docstring:
∑ᶠ x, f x is notation for finsum f. It is the sum of f x, where x ranges over the

conditions is possible, e.g. ∏ᶠ (x) (y), f x y and ∏ᶠ (x) (h: x ∈ s), f x

multiplicative support of f, if it's finite, one otherwise. Taking the product over multiple

concepts.name: LibraryNote.operator_precedence_of_big_operators
concepts.docstring:
There is no established mathematical convention
for the operator precedence of big operators like ∏ and ∑.
We will have to make a choice.
Online discussions, such as https://math.stackexchange.com/q/185538/30839
seem to suggest that ∏ and ∑ should have the same precedence,
and that this should be somewhere between * and +.
The latter have precedence levels 70 and 65 respectively,
and we therefore choose the level 67.
In practice, this means that parentheses should be placed as follows:
(Example taken from page 490 of Knuth's Concrete Mathematics.)

concepts.name: ModuleCat.extendScalars

l : M1 ⟶ M2 is sent to s ⊗ m ↦ s ⊗ l m

concepts.name: ModuleCat.CoextendScalars.obj'
concepts.docstring:
If M is an R-module, then the set of R-linear maps S →ₗ[R] M is an S-module with
scalar multiplication defined by s • l := x ↦ l (x • s).
This is an implementation detail: use (coextendScalars f).obj instead.

concepts.name: ModuleCat.CoextendScalars.map'
concepts.type_signature: obj' f M ⟶ obj' f M'
concepts.docstring:
If M, M' are R-modules, then any R-linear map g : M ⟶ M' induces an S-linear map
(S →ₗ[R] M) ⟶ (S →ₗ[R] M') defined by h ↦ g ∘ h

concepts.name: ModuleCat.coextendScalars
concepts.docstring:
For any rings R, S and a ring homomorphism f : R →+* S, there is a functor from R-module to
S-module defined by M ↦ (S →ₗ[R] M) where S is considered as an R-module via restriction of
scalars and g : M ⟶ M' is sent to h ↦ g ∘ h.
The definition of (coextendScalars f).obj is given by CoextendScalars.equiv.

concepts.name: ModuleCat.CoextendScalars.equiv
concepts.docstring:
The carrier of (coextendScalars f).obj M is S →ₗ[R] M where S is considered as an
R-module via restriction of scalars.

concepts.name: ModuleCat.RestrictionCoextensionAdj.HomEquiv.fromRestriction
concepts.docstring:
Given R-module X and S-module Y, any g : (restrictScalars f).obj Y ⟶ X
corresponds to Y ⟶ (coextendScalars f).obj X by sending y ↦ (s ↦ g (s • y))

concepts.name: ModuleCat.RestrictionCoextensionAdj.HomEquiv.toRestriction
concepts.docstring:
Given R-module X and S-module Y, any g : Y ⟶ (coextendScalars f).obj X
corresponds to (restrictScalars f).obj Y ⟶ X by y ↦ g y 1

concepts.name: ModuleCat.RestrictionCoextensionAdj.counit'

x ↦ g (1 ⊗ x).

concepts.name: ModuleCat.ExtendRestrictScalarsAdj.HomEquiv.evalAt
concepts.docstring: The map S → X →ₗ[R] Y given by fun s x => s • (g x)

s ⊗ x ↦ s • g x.

concepts.name: ModuleCat.ExtendRestrictScalarsAdj.Counit.map
