concepts.docstring:
The type of derivations with values in a B-module M relative
to a morphism f : A ⟶ B in the category CommRingCat.

concepts.name: ModuleCat.Derivation.mk
concepts.docstring: Constructor for ModuleCat.Derivation.

concepts.name: ModuleCat.Derivation.d
concepts.docstring:
The underlying map B → M of a derivation M.Derivation f when M : ModuleCat B
and f : A ⟶ B is a morphism in CommRingCat.

concepts.name: CommRingCat.KaehlerDifferential
concepts.docstring: The module of differentials of a morphism f : A ⟶ B in the category CommRingCat.

concepts.name: CommRingCat.KaehlerDifferential.D
concepts.docstring:
The (universal) derivation in (KaehlerDifferential f).Derivation f
when f : A ⟶ B is a morphism in the category CommRingCat.

concepts.name: CommRingCat.KaehlerDifferential.d
concepts.docstring:
When f : A ⟶ B is a morphism in the category CommRingCat, this is the
differential map B → KaehlerDifferential f.

concepts.name: CommRingCat.KaehlerDifferential.map
concepts.docstring:
The map KaehlerDifferential f ⟶ (ModuleCat.restrictScalars g').obj (KaehlerDifferential f')
induced by a commutative square (given by an equality g ≫ f' = f ≫ g')
in the category CommRingCat.

concepts.name: ModuleCat.Derivation.desc
concepts.docstring:
Given f : A ⟶ B a morphism in the category CommRingCat, M : ModuleCat B,
and D : M.Derivation f, this is the induced
morphism CommRingCat.KaehlerDifferential f ⟶ M.

concepts.name: PresheafOfModules.Derivation
concepts.docstring:
Given a morphism of presheaves of commutative rings φ : S ⟶ F.op ⋙ R,
this is the type of relative φ-derivation of a presheaf of R-modules M.

concepts.name: PresheafOfModules.Derivation.postcomp
concepts.docstring: The postcomposition of a derivation by a morphism of presheaves of modules.

concepts.name: PresheafOfModules.Derivation.Universal
concepts.docstring:
The universal property that a derivation d : M.Derivation φ must
satisfy so that the presheaf of modules M can be considered as the presheaf of
(relative) differentials of a presheaf of commutative rings φ : S ⟶ F.op ⋙ R.

concepts.name: PresheafOfModules.HasDifferentials
concepts.docstring:
The property that there exists a universal derivation for
a morphism of presheaves of commutative rings S ⟶ F.op ⋙ R.

concepts.name: PresheafOfModules.Derivation'
concepts.docstring:
Given a morphism of presheaves of commutative rings φ : S ⟶ R,
this is the type of relative φ-derivation of a presheaf of R-modules M.

concepts.name: PresheafOfModules.Derivation'.app
concepts.docstring:
The derivation relative to the morphism of commutative rings φ'.app X induced by
a derivation relative to a morphism of presheaves of commutative rings.

concepts.name: PresheafOfModules.Derivation'.mk
concepts.docstring:
Given a morphism of presheaves of commutative rings φ', this is the
in derivation M.Derivation' φ' that is given by a compatible family of derivations
with values in the modules M.obj X for all X.

concepts.name: PresheafOfModules.Derivation'.Universal.mk
concepts.docstring: Constructor for Derivation.Universal in the case F is the identity functor.

concepts.name: PresheafOfModules.DifferentialsConstruction.relativeDifferentials'
concepts.docstring:
The presheaf of relative differentials of a morphism of presheaves of
commutative rings.

concepts.name: PresheafOfModules.DifferentialsConstruction.derivation'
concepts.docstring: The universal derivation.

concepts.name: PresheafOfModules.DifferentialsConstruction.isUniversal'
concepts.docstring: The derivation Derivation' φ' is universal.

concepts.name: ModuleCat.uniqueOfEpiZero
concepts.docstring: If the zero morphism is an epi then the codomain is trivial.

concepts.name: ModuleCat.projectiveShortComplex
concepts.docstring: The standard short complex 0 → N → P → M → 0 with P= R^{⊕M} free.

concepts.name: ModuleCat.exteriorPower
concepts.docstring: The exterior power of an object in ModuleCat R.

concepts.name: ModuleCat.AlternatingMap
concepts.docstring: The type of n-alternating maps on M : ModuleCat R to N : ModuleCat R.

concepts.name: ModuleCat.AlternatingMap.postcomp
concepts.docstring: The postcomposition of an alternating map by a linear map.

concepts.name: ModuleCat.exteriorPower.mk
concepts.docstring:
Constructor for elements in M.exteriorPower n when M is an object of ModuleCat R
and n : ℕ.

concepts.name: ModuleCat.exteriorPower.desc
concepts.docstring: The morphism M.exteriorPower n ⟶ N induced by an alternating map.

concepts.name: ModuleCat.exteriorPower.map
concepts.docstring:
The morphism M.exteriorPower n ⟶ N.exteriorPower n induced by a morphism M ⟶ N
in ModuleCat R.

concepts.name: ModuleCat.exteriorPower.functor
concepts.docstring:
The functor ModuleCat R ⥤ ModuleCat R which sends a module to its
nth exterior power.

concepts.name: ModuleCat.exteriorPower.iso₀
concepts.docstring: The isomorphism M.exteriorPower 0 ≅ ModuleCat.of R R.

concepts.name: ModuleCat.exteriorPower.iso₁
concepts.docstring: The isomorphism M.exteriorPower 1 ≅ M.

concepts.name: ModuleCat.exteriorPower.natIso₀
concepts.docstring: The natural isomorphism M.exteriorPower 0 ≅ ModuleCat.of R R.

concepts.name: ModuleCat.exteriorPower.natIso₁
concepts.docstring: The natural isomorphism M.exteriorPower 1 ≅ M.

concepts.name: ModuleCat.FilteredColimits.M
concepts.docstring:
The colimit of F ⋙ forget₂ (ModuleCat R) AddCommGrpCat in the category AddCommGrpCat.
In the following, we will show that this has the structure of an R-module.

concepts.name: ModuleCat.FilteredColimits.M.mk
concepts.docstring: The canonical projection into the colimit, as a quotient type.

concepts.name: ModuleCat.FilteredColimits.colimitSMulAux
concepts.docstring: The "unlifted" version of scalar multiplication in the colimit.

concepts.name: ModuleCat.FilteredColimits.colimit
concepts.docstring: The bundled R-module giving the filtered colimit of a diagram.

concepts.name: ModuleCat.FilteredColimits.coconeMorphism
concepts.docstring: The linear map from a given R-module in the diagram to the colimit module.

concepts.name: ModuleCat.FilteredColimits.colimitCocone
concepts.docstring: The cocone over the proposed colimit module.

concepts.name: ModuleCat.FilteredColimits.colimitDesc
concepts.docstring:
Given a cocone t of F, the induced monoid linear map from the colimit to the cocone point.
We already know that this is a morphism between additive groups. The only thing left to see is that
it is a linear map, i.e. preserves scalar multiplication.

concepts.name: ModuleCat.FilteredColimits.colimitCoconeIsColimit
concepts.docstring: The proposed colimit cocone is a colimit in ModuleCat R.

concepts.name: ModuleCat.Basis.ofShortExact
concepts.docstring:
In a short exact sequence 0 ⟶ X₁ ⟶ X₂ ⟶ X₃ ⟶ 0, given bases for X₁ and X₃
indexed by ι and ι' respectively, we get a basis for X₂ indexed by ι ⊕ ι'.

concepts.name: ModuleCat.image
concepts.docstring: The image of a morphism in ModuleCat R is just the bundling of LinearMap.range f

concepts.name: ModuleCat.image.ι
concepts.docstring: The inclusion of image f into the target

concepts.name: ModuleCat.factorThruImage
concepts.docstring: The corestriction map to the image

concepts.name: ModuleCat.image.lift
concepts.docstring: The universal property for the image factorisation

concepts.name: ModuleCat.monoFactorisation
concepts.docstring: The factorisation of any morphism in ModuleCat R through a mono.

concepts.name: ModuleCat.isImage
concepts.docstring:
The factorisation of any morphism in ModuleCat R through a mono has the universal property of
the image.

concepts.name: ModuleCat.imageIsoRange
concepts.docstring: The categorical image of a morphism in ModuleCat R agrees with the linear algebraic range.

concepts.name: ModuleCat.kernelCone
concepts.docstring: The kernel cone induced by the concrete kernel.

concepts.name: ModuleCat.kernelIsLimit
concepts.docstring: The kernel of a linear map is a kernel in the categorical sense.

concepts.name: ModuleCat.isLimitKernelFork
concepts.docstring: Construct an IsLimit structure of kernels given Function.Exact.

concepts.name: ModuleCat.cokernelCocone
concepts.docstring: The cokernel cocone induced by the projection onto the quotient.

concepts.name: ModuleCat.cokernelIsColimit
concepts.docstring: The projection onto the quotient is a cokernel in the categorical sense.

concepts.name: ModuleCat.isColimitCokernelCofork
concepts.docstring: Construct an IsColimit structure of cokernels given Function.Exact.

concepts.name: ModuleCat.kernelIsoKer
concepts.docstring:
The categorical kernel of a morphism in ModuleCat
agrees with the usual module-theoretical kernel.

concepts.name: ModuleCat.cokernelIsoRangeQuotient
concepts.docstring:
The categorical cokernel of a morphism in ModuleCat
agrees with the usual module-theoretical quotient.

concepts.name: ModuleCat.projectiveResolution
concepts.docstring:
An R-module M can be functorially written as a quotient of a
projective R-module.

concepts.name: ModuleCat.sectionsSubmodule
concepts.docstring: The flat sections of a functor into ModuleCat R form a submodule of all sections.

concepts.name: ModuleCat.limitπLinearMap
concepts.docstring: limit.π (F ⋙ forget (ModuleCat.{w} R)) j as an R-linear map.

concepts.name: ModuleCat.HasLimits.limitCone
concepts.docstring:
Construction of a limit cone in ModuleCat R.
(Internal use only; use the limits API.)

concepts.name: ModuleCat.HasLimits.limitConeIsLimit
concepts.docstring:
Witness that the limit cone in ModuleCat R is a limit cone.
(Internal use only; use the limits API.)

concepts.name: ModuleCat.forget₂AddCommGroup_preservesLimitsAux
concepts.docstring: An auxiliary declaration to speed up typechecking.

concepts.name: ModuleCat.directLimitDiagram
concepts.docstring: The diagram (in the sense of CategoryTheory) of an unbundled directLimit of modules.

concepts.name: ModuleCat.directLimitCocone
concepts.docstring:
The Cocone on directLimitDiagram corresponding to
the unbundled directLimit of modules.
In directLimitIsColimit we show that it is a colimit cocone.

concepts.name: ModuleCat.directLimitIsColimit
concepts.docstring:
The unbundled directLimit of modules is a colimit
in the sense of CategoryTheory.

concepts.name: ModuleCat.localizedModule
concepts.docstring: Shrink of LocalizedModule S M in category which M belongs.

concepts.name: ModuleCat.localizedModuleMkLinearMap
concepts.docstring:
The linear map M →ₗ[R] (M.localizedModule S) which
exhibits M.localizedModule S as a localized module of M.

concepts.name: ModuleCat.localizedModuleMap
concepts.docstring: IsLocalizedModule.mapExtendScalars as a morphism in ModuleCat.

concepts.name: ModuleCat.localizedModuleFunctor
concepts.docstring:
The functor ModuleCat.{v} R ⥤ ModuleCat.{v} (Localization S) sending
M to M.localizedModule S and f : M1 ⟶ M2 to
IsLocalizedModule.mapExtendScalars S _ _ (Localization S) f.hom.

concepts.name: SemimoduleCat.MonoidalCategory.tensorObj
concepts.docstring: (implementation) tensor product of R-modules

concepts.name: SemimoduleCat.MonoidalCategory.tensorHom
concepts.type_signature: tensorObj M M' ⟶ tensorObj N N'
concepts.docstring: (implementation) tensor product of morphisms R-modules

concepts.name: SemimoduleCat.MonoidalCategory.whiskerLeft
concepts.type_signature: tensorObj M N₁ ⟶ tensorObj M N₂
concepts.docstring: (implementation) left whiskering for R-modules

concepts.name: SemimoduleCat.MonoidalCategory.whiskerRight
concepts.type_signature: tensorObj M₁ N ⟶ tensorObj M₂ N
concepts.docstring: (implementation) right whiskering for R-modules

concepts.name: SemimoduleCat.MonoidalCategory.associator
concepts.type_signature: tensorObj (tensorObj M N) K ≅ tensorObj M (tensorObj N K)
concepts.docstring: (implementation) the associator for R-modules

concepts.name: SemimoduleCat.MonoidalCategory.leftUnitor
concepts.docstring: (implementation) the left unitor for R-modules

concepts.name: SemimoduleCat.MonoidalCategory.rightUnitor
concepts.docstring: (implementation) the right unitor for R-modules

concepts.name: SemimoduleCat.MonoidalCategory.tensorLift
concepts.docstring: Construct for morphisms from the tensor product of two objects in SemimoduleCat.

concepts.name: ModuleCat.MonoidalCategory.tensorLift
concepts.docstring: Construct for morphisms from the tensor product of two objects in ModuleCat.

concepts.name: ModuleCat.monoidalClosedHomEquiv
concepts.type_signature: ((CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.tensorLeft M).obj N ⟶ P) ≃   (N ⟶ ((CategoryTheory.linearCoyoneda R (ModuleCat R)).obj (Opposite.op M)).obj P)
concepts.docstring:
Auxiliary definition for the MonoidalClosed instance on Module R.
(This is only a separate definition in order to speed up typechecking.)

concepts.name: SemimoduleCat.braiding
concepts.docstring: (implementation) the braiding for R-modules

concepts.name: PresheafOfModules.restrictScalarsObj
concepts.docstring: The restriction of scalars of presheaves of modules, on objects.

concepts.name: PresheafOfModules.restrictScalars
concepts.docstring:
The restriction of scalars functor PresheafOfModules R' ⥤ PresheafOfModules R
induced by a morphism of presheaves of rings R ⟶ R'.

concepts.name: PresheafOfModules.restrictScalarsCompToPresheaf
concepts.docstring:
The isomorphism restrictScalars α ⋙ toPresheaf R ≅ toPresheaf R' for any
morphism of presheaves of rings α : R ⟶ R'.

concepts.name: PresheafOfModules.constFunctor
concepts.docstring:
Given a cocone cR for a functor R : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ RingCat, this is the
functor ModuleCat cR.pt ⥤ PresheafOfModules R which sends a module M
over cR.pt to a presheaf of modules whose underlying presheaf of
abelian groups is the constant functor Cᵒᵖ ⥤ AddCommGrpCat with value M.

concepts.name: PresheafOfModules.ModuleColimit
concepts.type_signature: CategoryTheory.Limits.IsColimit cR → CategoryTheory.Limits.IsColimit cM → Type w
concepts.docstring:
Given a colimit cocone for a presheaf of rings R on a cofiltered category C,
M a presheaf of modules over R, and a colimit cocone cM for the underlying
functor Cᵒᵖ ⥤ AddCommGrpCat of M, this is the type cM.pt on which we define
a module structure below.

concepts.name: PresheafOfModules.ModuleColimit.coconeSMul
concepts.docstring:
The cocone for R ⋙ forget _ ⊗ M.presheaf ⋙ forget _ with point
ModuleColimit hcR hcM which allows to define the scalar multiplication
by cR.pt on ModuleColimit hcR hcM.

concepts.name: PresheafOfModules.ModuleColimit.ιR
concepts.docstring: The "inclusion" maps to the colimit ring.

concepts.name: PresheafOfModules.ModuleColimit.ιM
concepts.docstring: The "inclusion" maps to the colimit module, as an additive map.

concepts.name: PresheafOfModules.ModuleColimit.homEquiv'
concepts.docstring:
Auxiliary definition for homEquiv. This is the universal property
of PresheafOfModules.ModuleColimit, as an abelian group.

concepts.name: PresheafOfModules.ModuleColimit.homEquiv
concepts.docstring:
This is the universal property of PresheafOfModules.ModuleColimit as a module.
See also PresheafOfModules.colimitAdjunction.

concepts.name: PresheafOfModules.ModuleColimit.map
concepts.type_signature: ModuleColimit hcR hcM →ₗ[↑cR.pt] ModuleColimit hcR hcM'
concepts.docstring: The linear map between the colimit modules induced by a morphism of modules.

concepts.name: PresheafOfModules.colimitFunctor
concepts.docstring:
The colimit module functor from the category of presheaves of modules
over a presheaf of rings R on a cofiltered category to the category
of modules over a colimit of R.

concepts.name: PresheafOfModules.colimitAdjunction
concepts.docstring:
Given a presheaf of rings R on a cofiltered category, this is the
adjunction between colimitFunctor : PresheafOfModules R ⥤ ModuleCat cR.pt
and the constant functor.

concepts.name: PresheafOfModules.evaluationJointlyReflectsColimits
concepts.docstring:
A cocone in the category PresheafOfModules R is colimit if it is so after the application
of the functors evaluation R X for all X.

concepts.name: PresheafOfModules.colimitPresheafOfModules
concepts.docstring:
Given F : J ⥤ PresheafOfModules.{v} R, this is the presheaf of modules obtained by
taking a colimit in the category of modules over R.obj X for all X.

concepts.name: PresheafOfModules.colimitCocone
concepts.docstring:
The (colimit) cocone for F : J ⥤ PresheafOfModules.{v} R that is constructed from
the colimit of F ⋙ evaluation R X for all X.

concepts.name: PresheafOfModules.isColimitColimitCocone
concepts.docstring: The cocone colimitCocone F is colimit for any F : J ⥤ PresheafOfModules.{v} R.

concepts.name: PresheafOfModules.freeObj
concepts.docstring:
Given a presheaf of types F : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u, this is the presheaf
of modules over R which sends X : Cᵒᵖ to the free R.obj X-module on F.obj X.

concepts.name: PresheafOfModules.free
concepts.docstring: The free presheaf of modules functor (Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) ⥤ PresheafOfModules.{u} R.

concepts.name: PresheafOfModules.freeObjDesc
concepts.docstring:
The morphism of presheaves of modules freeObj F ⟶ G corresponding to
a morphism F ⟶ G.presheaf ⋙ forget _ of presheaves of types.

concepts.name: PresheafOfModules.freeAdjunctionUnit
concepts.docstring: The unit of PresheafOfModules.freeAdjunction.

concepts.name: PresheafOfModules.freeHomEquiv
concepts.docstring:
The bijection (freeObj F ⟶ G) ≃ (F ⟶ G.presheaf ⋙ forget _) when
F is a presheaf of types and G a presheaf of modules.

concepts.name: PresheafOfModules.freeAdjunction
concepts.type_signature: free R ⊣ (toPresheaf R).comp ((CategoryTheory.Functor.whiskeringRight Cᵒᵖ Ab (Type u)).obj (CategoryTheory.forget Ab))
concepts.docstring:
The free presheaf of modules functor is left adjoint to the forget functor
PresheafOfModules.{u} R ⥤ Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u.

concepts.name: PresheafOfModules.freeYonedaEquiv
concepts.docstring:
When R : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ RingCat, M : PresheafOfModules R, and X : C, this is the
bijection ((free R).obj (yoneda.obj X) ⟶ M) ≃ M.obj (Opposite.op X).

concepts.name: PresheafOfModules.freeYoneda
concepts.docstring:
The set of PresheafOfModules.{v} R consisting of objects of the
form (free R).obj (yoneda.obj X) for some X.

concepts.name: PresheafOfModules.Elements
concepts.docstring:
The type of elements of a presheaf of modules. A term of this type is a pair
⟨X, a⟩ with X : Cᵒᵖ and a : M.obj X.

concepts.name: PresheafOfModules.elementsMk
concepts.docstring: Given a presheaf of modules M, this is a constructor for the type M.Elements.

concepts.name: PresheafOfModules.Elements.freeYoneda
concepts.docstring:
Given an element m : M.Elements of a presheaf of modules M, this is the
free presheaf of modules on the Yoneda presheaf of types corresponding to the
underlying object of m.

concepts.name: PresheafOfModules.Elements.fromFreeYoneda
concepts.docstring:
Given an element m : M.Elements of a presheaf of modules M, this is
the canonical morphism m.freeYoneda ⟶ M.

concepts.name: PresheafOfModules.freeYonedaCoproduct
concepts.docstring:
Given a presheaf of modules M, this is the coproduct of
all free Yoneda presheaves m.freeYoneda for all m : M.Elements.

concepts.name: PresheafOfModules.ιFreeYonedaCoproduct
concepts.docstring:
Given an element m : M.Elements of a presheaf of modules M, this is the
canonical inclusion m.freeYoneda ⟶ M.freeYonedaCoproduct.

concepts.name: PresheafOfModules.fromFreeYonedaCoproduct
concepts.docstring:
Given a presheaf of modules M, this is the
canonical morphism M.freeYonedaCoproduct ⟶ M.

concepts.name: PresheafOfModules.freeYonedaCoproductMk
concepts.docstring:
Given an element m of a presheaf of modules M, this is the associated
canonical section of the presheaf M.freeYonedaCoproduct over the object m.1.

concepts.name: PresheafOfModules.toFreeYonedaCoproduct
concepts.docstring:
Given a presheaf of modules M, this is a morphism between coproducts
of free presheaves of modules on Yoneda presheaves which gives a presentation
of the module M, see isColimitFreeYonedaCoproductsCokernelCofork.

concepts.name: PresheafOfModules.freeYonedaCoproductsCokernelCofork
concepts.docstring:
(Colimit) cofork which gives a presentation of a presheaf of modules M using
coproducts of free presheaves of modules on Yoneda presheaves.

concepts.name: PresheafOfModules.isColimitFreeYonedaCoproductsCokernelCofork
concepts.docstring:
If M is a presheaf of modules, the cokernel cofork
M.freeYonedaCoproductsCokernelCofork is a colimit, which means that
M can be expressed as a cokernel of the morphism M.toFreeYonedaCoproduct
between coproducts of free presheaves of modules on Yoneda presheaves.

concepts.name: PresheafOfModules.evaluationJointlyReflectsLimits
concepts.docstring:
A cone in the category PresheafOfModules R is limit if it is so after the application
of the functors evaluation R X for all X.

concepts.name: PresheafOfModules.limitPresheafOfModules
concepts.docstring:
Given F : J ⥤ PresheafOfModules.{v} R, this is the presheaf of modules obtained by
taking a limit in the category of modules over R.obj X for all X.

concepts.name: PresheafOfModules.limitCone
concepts.docstring:
The (limit) cone for F : J ⥤ PresheafOfModules.{v} R that is constructed from the limit
of F ⋙ evaluation R X for all X.

concepts.name: PresheafOfModules.isLimitLimitCone
concepts.docstring: The cone limitCone F is limit for any F : J ⥤ PresheafOfModules.{v} R.

concepts.name: PresheafOfModules.Monoidal.tensorObjMap
concepts.docstring: Auxiliary definition for tensorObj.

concepts.name: PresheafOfModules.Monoidal.tensorObj
concepts.docstring: The tensor product of two presheaves of modules.

concepts.name: PresheafOfModules.Monoidal.tensorHom
concepts.type_signature: tensorObj M₁ M₃ ⟶ tensorObj M₂ M₄
concepts.docstring: The tensor product of two morphisms of presheaves of modules.

concepts.name: PresheafOfModules.pullback
concepts.docstring:
The pullback functor PresheafOfModules S ⥤ PresheafOfModules R induced by
a morphism of presheaves of rings S ⟶ F.op ⋙ R, defined as the left adjoint
functor to the pushforward, when it exists.

concepts.name: PresheafOfModules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction
concepts.docstring:
Given a morphism of presheaves of rings S ⟶ F.op ⋙ R, this is the adjunction
between associated pullback and pushforward functors on the categories
of presheaves of modules.

concepts.name: PresheafOfModules.pullbackObjIsDefined
concepts.docstring:
Given a morphism of presheaves of rings φ : S ⟶ F.op ⋙ R, this is the property
that the (partial) left adjoint functor of pushforward φ is defined
on a certain object M : PresheafOfModules S.

concepts.name: PresheafOfModules.pushforwardCompCoyonedaFreeYonedaCorepresentableBy
concepts.docstring:
Given a morphism of presheaves of rings φ : S ⟶ F.op ⋙ R, where F : C ⥤ D,
S : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ RingCat, R : Dᵒᵖ ⥤ RingCat and X : C, the (partial) left adjoint
functor of pushforward φ is defined on the object (free S).obj (yoneda.obj X):
this object shall be mapped to (free R).obj (yoneda.obj (F.obj X)).

concepts.name: PresheafOfModules.pullbackId
concepts.docstring:
The pullback by the identity morphism identifies to the identity functor of the
category of presheaves of modules.

concepts.name: PresheafOfModules.pullbackComp
concepts.docstring:
The composition of two pullback functors on presheaves of modules identifies
to the pullback for the composition.

concepts.name: PresheafOfModules.pushforward₀Obj
concepts.docstring: Implementation of pushforward₀.

concepts.name: PresheafOfModules.pushforward₀_obj
concepts.docstring:
Alias of PresheafOfModules.pushforward₀Obj.
Implementation of pushforward₀.

concepts.name: PresheafOfModules.pushforward₀
concepts.docstring:
The pushforward functor on presheaves of modules for a functor F : C ⥤ D and
R : Dᵒᵖ ⥤ RingCat. On the underlying presheaves of abelian groups, it is induced
by the precomposition with F.op.

concepts.name: PresheafOfModules.pushforward₀OfCommRingCat
concepts.type_signature:
CategoryTheory.Functor (PresheafOfModules (R.comp (CategoryTheory.forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat)))
(PresheafOfModules ((F.op.comp R).comp (CategoryTheory.forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat)))
concepts.docstring:
If F : C ⥤ D if a functor and R : Dᵒᵖ ⥤ CommRingCat is a presheaf
of commutative rings, this is the pushforward functor from the category
of presheaves of modules on R to the category of presheaves of
modules on F.op ⋙ R.

concepts.name: PresheafOfModules.pushforward₀CompToPresheaf
concepts.type_signature: (pushforward₀ F R).comp (toPresheaf (F.op.comp R)) ≅ (toPresheaf R).comp ((CategoryTheory.Functor.whiskeringLeft Cᵒᵖ Dᵒᵖ Ab).obj F.op)
concepts.docstring:
The pushforward of presheaves of modules commutes with the forgetful functor
to presheaves of abelian groups.

concepts.name: PresheafOfModules.pushforward
concepts.docstring:
The pushforward functor PresheafOfModules R ⥤ PresheafOfModules S induced by
a morphism of presheaves of rings S ⟶ F.op ⋙ R.

concepts.name: PresheafOfModules.pushforwardCompToPresheaf
concepts.type_signature: (pushforward φ).comp (toPresheaf S) ≅ (toPresheaf R).comp ((CategoryTheory.Functor.whiskeringLeft Cᵒᵖ Dᵒᵖ Ab).obj F.op)
concepts.docstring:
The pushforward of presheaves of modules commutes with the forgetful functor
to presheaves of abelian groups.

concepts.name: PresheafOfModules.pushforwardId
concepts.docstring:
The pushforward functor by the identity morphism identifies to
the identify functor of the category of presheaves of modules.

concepts.name: PresheafOfModules.pushforwardComp
concepts.docstring:
The composition of two pushforward functors on categories of presheaves of modules
identify to the pushforward for the composition.

concepts.name: PresheafOfModules.sheafification
concepts.docstring:
Given a locally bijective morphism α : R₀ ⟶ R.val where R₀ is a presheaf of rings
and R a sheaf of rings (i.e. R identifies to the sheafification of R₀), this is
the associated sheaf of modules functor PresheafOfModules.{v} R₀ ⥤ SheafOfModules.{v} R.

concepts.name: PresheafOfModules.sheafificationCompToSheaf
concepts.docstring:
The sheafification of presheaves of modules commutes with the functor which
forgets the module structures.

concepts.name: PresheafOfModules.sheafificationCompForgetCompToPresheaf
concepts.type_signature:
(sheafification α).comp ((SheafOfModules.forget R).comp (toPresheaf R.obj)) ≅ (toPresheaf R₀).comp
((CategoryTheory.presheafToSheaf J AddCommGrpCat).comp (CategoryTheory.sheafToPresheaf J AddCommGrpCat))
concepts.docstring:
The sheafification of presheaves of modules commutes with the functor which
forgets the module structures.

concepts.name: PresheafOfModules.sheafificationHomEquiv
concepts.type_signature: ((sheafification α).obj P ⟶ F) ≃ (P ⟶ (restrictScalars α).obj ((SheafOfModules.forget R).obj F))
concepts.docstring:
The bijection between types of morphisms which is part of the adjunction
sheafificationAdjunction.

concepts.name: PresheafOfModules.sheafificationAdjunction
concepts.docstring:
Given a locally bijective morphism α : R₀ ⟶ R.val where R₀ is a presheaf of rings
and R a sheaf of rings, this is the adjunction
sheafification.{v} α ⊣ SheafOfModules.forget R ⋙ restrictScalars α.

concepts.name: CategoryTheory.Presieve.FamilyOfElements.smul
concepts.docstring:
The scalar multiplication of family of elements of a presheaf of modules M over R
by a family of elements of R.

concepts.name: PresheafOfModules.Sheafify.SMulCandidate
concepts.docstring:
Assuming α : R₀ ⟶ R.val is the sheafification map of a presheaf of rings R₀
and φ : M₀.presheaf ⟶ A.val is the sheafification map of the underlying
sheaf of abelian groups of a presheaf of modules M₀ over R₀, then given
r : R.val.obj X and m : A.val.obj X, this structure contains the data
of x : A.val.obj X along with the property which makes x a good candidate
for the definition of the scalar multiplication r • m.

concepts.name: PresheafOfModules.Sheafify.SMulCandidate.mk'
concepts.docstring: Constructor for SMulCandidate.

concepts.name: PresheafOfModules.Sheafify.smulCandidate
concepts.docstring: The (unique) element in SMulCandidate α φ r m.

concepts.name: PresheafOfModules.Sheafify.smul
concepts.docstring: The scalar multiplication on the sheafification of a presheaf of modules.

concepts.name: PresheafOfModules.Sheafify.module
concepts.docstring:
The module structure on the sections of the sheafification of the underlying
presheaf of abelian groups of a presheaf of modules.

concepts.name: PresheafOfModules.sheafify
concepts.docstring:
Assuming α : R₀ ⟶ R.obj is the sheafification map of a presheaf of rings R₀
and φ : M₀.presheaf ⟶ A.obj is the sheafification map of the underlying
sheaf of abelian groups of a presheaf of modules M₀ over R₀, this is
the sheaf of modules over R which is obtained by endowing the sections of
A.obj with a scalar multiplication.

concepts.name: PresheafOfModules.toSheafify
concepts.docstring: The canonical morphism from a presheaf of modules to its associated sheaf.

concepts.name: PresheafOfModules.sheafifyHomEquiv'
concepts.docstring:
The bijection ((sheafify α φ).val ⟶ F) ≃ (M₀ ⟶ (restrictScalars α).obj F) which
is part of the universal property of the sheafification of the presheaf of modules M₀,
when F is a presheaf of modules which is a sheaf.

concepts.name: PresheafOfModules.sheafifyHomEquiv
concepts.type_signature: (sheafify α φ ⟶ F) ≃ (M₀ ⟶ (restrictScalars α).obj ((SheafOfModules.forget R).obj F))
concepts.docstring:
The bijection
(sheafify α φ ⟶ F) ≃ (M₀ ⟶ (restrictScalars α).obj ((SheafOfModules.forget _).obj F))
which is part of the universal property of the sheafification of the presheaf of modules M₀,
for any sheaf of modules F, see PresheafOfModules.sheafificationAdjunction

concepts.name: PresheafOfModules.sheafifyMap
concepts.type_signature: sheafify α φ ⟶ sheafify α φ'
concepts.docstring:
The morphism of sheaves of modules sheafify α φ ⟶ sheafify α φ'
induced by morphisms τ₀ : M₀ ⟶ M₀' and τ : A ⟶ A'
which satisfy τ₀.hom ≫ φ' = φ ≫ τ.val.

concepts.name: PresheafOfModules
concepts.docstring:
A presheaf of modules over R : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ RingCat consists of family of
objects obj X : ModuleCat (R.obj X) for all X : Cᵒᵖ together with
functorial maps obj X ⟶ (ModuleCat.restrictScalars (R.map f)).obj (obj Y)
for all f : X ⟶ Y in Cᵒᵖ.

concepts.name: PresheafOfModules.Hom
concepts.docstring:
A morphism of presheaves of modules consists of a family of linear maps which
satisfy the naturality condition.

concepts.name: PresheafOfModules.isoMk
concepts.docstring: Constructor for isomorphisms in the category of presheaves of modules.

concepts.name: PresheafOfModules.presheaf
concepts.docstring: The underlying presheaf of abelian groups of a presheaf of modules.

concepts.name: PresheafOfModules.toPresheaf
concepts.docstring: The forgetful functor PresheafOfModules R ⥤ Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Ab.

concepts.name: PresheafOfModules.ofPresheaf
concepts.docstring:
The object in PresheafOfModules R that is obtained from M : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Ab.{v} such
that for all X : Cᵒᵖ, M.obj X is a R.obj X module, in such a way that the
restriction maps are semilinear. (This constructor should be used only in cases
when the preferred constructor PresheafOfModules.mk is not as convenient as this one.)

concepts.name: PresheafOfModules.homMk
concepts.docstring:
The morphism of presheaves of modules M₁ ⟶ M₂ given by a morphism
of abelian presheaves M₁.presheaf ⟶ M₂.presheaf
which satisfy a suitable linearity condition.

concepts.name: PresheafOfModules.evaluation
concepts.docstring:
Evaluation on an object X gives a functor
PresheafOfModules R ⥤ ModuleCat (R.obj X).

concepts.name: PresheafOfModules.restriction
concepts.type_signature: evaluation R X ⟶ (evaluation R Y).comp (ModuleCat.restrictScalars (RingCat.Hom.hom (R.map f)))
concepts.docstring:
The restriction natural transformation on presheaves of modules, considered as linear maps
to restriction of scalars.

concepts.name: PresheafOfModules.unit
concepts.docstring: The obvious free presheaf of modules of rank 1.

concepts.name: PresheafOfModules.sections
concepts.docstring: The type of sections of a presheaf of modules.

concepts.name: PresheafOfModules.sections.eval
concepts.docstring:
Given a presheaf of modules M, s : M.sections and X : Cᵒᵖ, this is the induced
element in M.obj X.

concepts.name: PresheafOfModules.sectionsMk
concepts.docstring: Constructor for sections of a presheaf of modules.

concepts.name: PresheafOfModules.sectionsMap
concepts.docstring: The map M.sections → N.sections induced by a morphisms M ⟶ N of presheaves of modules.

concepts.name: PresheafOfModules.unitHomEquiv
concepts.docstring: The bijection (unit R ⟶ M) ≃ M.sections for M : PresheafOfModules R.

concepts.name: PresheafOfModules.forgetToPresheafModuleCatObjObj
concepts.docstring: Auxiliary definition for forgetToPresheafModuleCatObj.

concepts.name: PresheafOfModules.forgetToPresheafModuleCatObjMap
concepts.type_signature: forgetToPresheafModuleCatObjObj X hX M Y ⟶ forgetToPresheafModuleCatObjObj X hX M Z
concepts.docstring: Auxiliary definition for forgetToPresheafModuleCatObj.

concepts.name: PresheafOfModules.forgetToPresheafModuleCatObj
concepts.docstring:
Implementation of the functor PresheafOfModules R ⥤ Cᵒᵖ ⥤ ModuleCat (R.obj X)
when X is initial.
The functor is implemented as, on object level M ↦ (c ↦ M(c)) where the R(X)-module structure
on M(c) is given by restriction of scalars along the unique morphism R(c) ⟶ R(X); and on
morphism level (f : M ⟶ N) ↦ (c ↦ f(c)).

concepts.name: PresheafOfModules.forgetToPresheafModuleCatMap
concepts.type_signature: forgetToPresheafModuleCatObj X hX M ⟶ forgetToPresheafModuleCatObj X hX N
concepts.docstring:
Implementation of the functor PresheafOfModules R ⥤ Cᵒᵖ ⥤ ModuleCat (R.obj X)
when X is initial.
The functor is implemented as, on object level M ↦ (c ↦ M(c)) where the R(X)-module structure
on M(c) is given by restriction of scalars along the unique morphism R(c) ⟶ R(X); and on
morphism level (f : M ⟶ N) ↦ (c ↦ f(c)).

concepts.name: PresheafOfModules.forgetToPresheafModuleCat
concepts.docstring:
The forgetful functor from presheaves of modules over a presheaf of rings R to presheaves of
R(X)-modules where X is an initial object.
The functor is implemented as, on object level M ↦ (c ↦ M(c)) where the R(X)-module structure
on M(c) is given by restriction of scalars along the unique morphism R(c) ⟶ R(X); and on
morphism level (f : M ⟶ N) ↦ (c ↦ f(c)).

concepts.name: ModuleCat.productCone
concepts.docstring: The product cone induced by the concrete product.

concepts.name: ModuleCat.productConeIsLimit
concepts.docstring: The concrete product cone is limiting.

concepts.name: ModuleCat.piIsoPi
concepts.docstring:
The categorical product of a family of objects in ModuleCat
agrees with the usual module-theoretical product.

concepts.name: ModuleCat.coproductCocone
concepts.docstring: The coproduct cone induced by the concrete coproduct.

concepts.name: ModuleCat.coproductCoconeIsColimit
concepts.docstring: The concrete coproduct cone is colimiting.

concepts.name: ModuleCat.coprodIsoDirectSum
concepts.type_signature: ∐ Z ≅ of R (DirectSum ι fun (i : ι) => ↑(Z i))
concepts.docstring:
The categorical coproduct of a family of objects in ModuleCat

concepts.name: CommRingCat.moduleCatRestrictScalarsPseudofunctor
concepts.docstring:
The pseudofunctor from LocallyDiscrete CommRingCatᵒᵖ to Cat which sends
a commutative ring R to its category of modules. The functoriality is given by
the restriction of scalars.

concepts.name: RingCat.moduleCatRestrictScalarsPseudofunctor
concepts.docstring:
The pseudofunctor from LocallyDiscrete RingCatᵒᵖ to Cat which sends a ring R
to its category of modules. The functoriality is given by the restriction of scalars.

concepts.name: CommRingCat.moduleCatExtendScalarsPseudofunctor
concepts.docstring:
The pseudofunctor from LocallyDiscrete CommRingCat to Cat which sends
a commutative ring R to its category of modules. The functoriality is given by
the extension of scalars.

concepts.name: SemimoduleCat
concepts.docstring:
The category of R-semimodules and their morphisms.
Note that in the case of R = ℕ, we can not
impose here that the ℕ-multiplication field from the module structure is defeq to the one coming
from the isAddCommMonoid structure (contrary to what we do for all module structures in
mathlib), which creates some difficulties down the road.

concepts.name: SemimoduleCat.of
concepts.docstring:
The object in the category of R-algebras associated to a type equipped with the appropriate
typeclasses. This is the preferred way to construct a term of SemimoduleCat R.

concepts.name: SemimoduleCat.Hom
concepts.docstring: The type of morphisms in SemimoduleCat R.

concepts.name: SemimoduleCat.Hom.hom
concepts.docstring: Turn a morphism in SemimoduleCat back into a LinearMap.

concepts.name: SemimoduleCat.ofHom
concepts.type_signature: of R X ⟶ of R Y

concepts.name: SemimoduleCat.Hom.Simps.hom
concepts.docstring: Use the ConcreteCategory.hom projection for @[simps] lemmas.

concepts.name: SemimoduleCat.homEquiv
concepts.docstring: SemimoduleCat.Hom.hom bundled as an Equiv.

concepts.name: SemimoduleCat.«term↟_»
concepts.docstring: Reinterpreting a linear map in the category of R-modules

concepts.name: LinearEquiv.toModuleIsoₛ
concepts.type_signature: SemimoduleCat.of R X₁ ≅ SemimoduleCat.of R X₂
concepts.docstring: Build an isomorphism in the category Module R from a LinearEquiv between Modules.

concepts.name: CategoryTheory.Iso.toLinearEquivₛ

concepts.name: linearEquivIsoModuleIsoₛ
concepts.type_signature: (X ≃ₗ[R] Y) ≅ SemimoduleCat.of R X ≅ SemimoduleCat.of R Y

linear equivalences between Modules are the same as (isomorphic to) isomorphisms

concepts.name: SemimoduleCat.homAddEquiv
concepts.docstring: SemimoduleCat.Hom.hom bundled as an additive equivalence.

concepts.name: SemimoduleCat.homLinearEquiv
concepts.docstring: SemimoduleCat.Hom.hom bundled as a linear equivalence.

concepts.name: SemimoduleCat.Algebra.instModuleCarrier
concepts.docstring: Let S be an S₀-algebra. Then S-modules are modules over S₀.

concepts.name: SemimoduleCat.ofHom₂
concepts.docstring: Turn a bilinear map into a homomorphism.

concepts.name: SemimoduleCat.Hom.hom₂
concepts.docstring: Turn a homomorphism into a bilinear map.

concepts.name: SheafOfModules.restrictScalars
concepts.docstring:
The restriction of scalars functor SheafOfModules R' ⥤ SheafOfModules R
induced by a morphism of sheaves of rings R ⟶ R'.

concepts.name: PresheafOfModules.restrictHomEquivOfIsLocallySurjective
concepts.docstring:
The functor PresheafOfModules.restrictScalars α induces bijections on
morphisms if α is locally surjective and the target presheaf is a sheaf.

concepts.name: SheafOfModules.free
concepts.docstring: The free sheaf of modules on a certain type I.

concepts.name: SheafOfModules.ιFree
concepts.docstring: The inclusions unit R ⟶ free I.

concepts.name: SheafOfModules.freeCofan
concepts.docstring: The tautological cofan with point free I : SheafOfModules R.

concepts.name: SheafOfModules.isColimitFreeCofan
concepts.docstring: free I is the colimit of copies of unit R indexed by I.

concepts.name: SheafOfModules.freeHomEquiv
concepts.docstring:
The data of a morphism free I ⟶ M from a free sheaf of modules is
equivalent to the data of a family I → M.sections of sections of M.

concepts.name: SheafOfModules.freeSection
concepts.docstring: The tautological section of free I : SheafOfModules R corresponding to i : I.

concepts.name: SheafOfModules.freeMap
concepts.docstring:
The morphism of presheaves of R-modules free I ⟶ free J induced by
a map f : I → J.

concepts.name: SheafOfModules.freeFunctor
concepts.docstring:
The functor Type u ⥤ SheafOfModules.{u} R which sends a type I to
free I which is a coproduct indexed by I of copies of R (thought of as a
presheaf of modules over itself).

concepts.name: SheafOfModules.freeSumIso
concepts.type_signature: free I ⨿ free J✝ ≅ free (I ⊕ J✝)
concepts.docstring:
A binary coproduct of free sheaves of modules is the free sheaf
of modules on the sum type.

concepts.name: SheafOfModules.mapFree
concepts.docstring:
Let F be a functor from the category of sheaves of R-modules to sheaves of S-modules.
Then a morphism η : unit S ⟶ F.obj (unit R) induces a morphism from free (R := S) I to
F.obj (free I). See also mapFreeIso for the iso version.

concepts.name: SheafOfModules.mapFreeIso
concepts.docstring:
Let F be a functor from the category of sheaves of R-modules to sheaves of S-modules.
If F preserves coproducts and unit S ≅ F.obj (unit R), then F preserves free sheaves of
modules.

concepts.name: SheafOfModules.GeneratingSections
concepts.docstring: The type of sections which generate a sheaf of modules.

concepts.name: SheafOfModules.GeneratingSections.π
concepts.docstring: The epimorphism free σ.I ⟶ M given by σ : M.GeneratingSections.

concepts.name: SheafOfModules.GeneratingSections.ofEpi
concepts.docstring:
If M ⟶ N is an epimorphism and that M is generated by some sections,
then N is generated by the images of these sections.

concepts.name: SheafOfModules.GeneratingSections.equivOfIso
concepts.docstring: Two isomorphic sheaves of modules have equivalent families of generating sections.

concepts.name: SheafOfModules.GeneratingSections.IsFiniteType
concepts.docstring: σ : M.GeneratingSections is finite type if the index type σ.I is finite.

concepts.name: SheafOfModules.LocalGeneratorsData
concepts.docstring:
The data of generating sections of the restriction of a sheaf of modules
over a covering of the terminal object.

concepts.name: SheafOfModules.LocalGeneratorsData.shrink
concepts.docstring: Shrink the indexing type of LocalGeneratorsData into the universe of the site.

concepts.name: SheafOfModules.LocalGeneratorsData.IsFiniteType
concepts.docstring:
The data of local generators of a sheaf of modules is finite type if
each family of generators is finite type.

concepts.name: SheafOfModules.IsFiniteType
concepts.docstring:
A sheaf of modules is of finite type if locally, it is generated by finitely
many sections.

concepts.name: SheafOfModules
concepts.docstring:
A sheaf of modules is a presheaf of modules such that the underlying presheaf
of abelian groups is a sheaf.

concepts.name: SheafOfModules.Hom
concepts.docstring:
A morphism between sheaves of modules is a morphism between the underlying
presheaves of modules.

concepts.name: SheafOfModules.forget
concepts.docstring: The forgetful functor SheafOfModules.{v} R ⥤ PresheafOfModules R.val.

concepts.name: SheafOfModules.fullyFaithfulForget
concepts.docstring: The forget functor SheafOfModules R ⥤ PresheafOfModules R.val is fully faithful.

concepts.name: SheafOfModules.evaluation
concepts.docstring:
Evaluation on an object X gives a functor
SheafOfModules R ⥤ ModuleCat (R.val.obj X).

concepts.name: SheafOfModules.toSheaf
concepts.docstring: The forget functor SheafOfModules R ⥤ Sheaf J AddCommGrpCat.

concepts.name: SheafOfModules.forgetToSheafModuleCat
concepts.docstring:
The forgetful functor from sheaves of modules over sheaf of ring R to sheaves of R(X)-module
when X is initial.

concepts.name: SheafOfModules.toSheafCompSheafToPresheafIso
SheafOfModules.sections
concepts.docstring: The type of sections of a sheaf of modules.

concepts.name: SheafOfModules.sectionsMap
concepts.docstring: The map M.sections → N.sections induced by a morphism M ⟶ N of sheaves of modules.

concepts.name: SheafOfModules.sectionsFunctor
concepts.docstring: The functor which sends a sheaf of modules to its type of sections.

concepts.name: SheafOfModules.unit
concepts.docstring: The obvious free sheaf of modules of rank 1.

concepts.name: SheafOfModules.unitHomEquiv
concepts.docstring: The bijection (unit R ⟶ M) ≃ M.sections for M : SheafOfModules R.

concepts.name: PresheafOfModules.IsLocallySurjective
concepts.docstring:
A morphism of presheaves of modules is locally surjective
if the underlying morphism of presheaves of abelian groups is.

concepts.name: PresheafOfModules.IsLocallyInjective
concepts.docstring:
A morphism of presheaves of modules is locally injective
if the underlying morphism of presheaves of abelian groups is.

concepts.name: PresheafOfModules.homEquivOfIsLocallyBijective
concepts.docstring:
The bijection (M₂ ⟶ N) ≃ (M₁ ⟶ N) induced by a locally bijective morphism
f : M₁ ⟶ M₂ of presheaves of modules, when N is a sheaf.

concepts.name: NNRat.castRec
concepts.docstring:
The default definition of the coercion ℚ≥0 → K for a division semiring K.
↑q : K is defined as (q.num : K) / (q.den : K).
Do not use this directly (instances of DivisionSemiring are allowed to override that default for
better definitional properties). Instead, use the coercion.

concepts.name: Rat.castRec
concepts.docstring:
The default definition of the coercion ℚ → K for a division ring K.
↑q : K is defined as (q.num : K) / (q.den : K).
Do not use this directly (instances of DivisionRing are allowed to override that default for
better definitional properties). Instead, use the coercion.

concepts.name: DivisionSemiring
concepts.docstring:
A DivisionSemiring is a Semiring with multiplicative inverses for nonzero elements.
An instance of DivisionSemiring K includes maps nnratCast : ℚ≥0 → K and nnqsmul : ℚ≥0 → K → K.
Those two fields are needed to implement the DivisionSemiring K → Algebra ℚ≥0 K instance since we
need to control the specific definitions for some special cases of K (in particular K = ℚ≥0
itself). See also note [forgetful inheritance].
If the division semiring has positive characteristic p, our division by zero convention forces
nnratCast (1 / p) = 1 / 0 = 0.

concepts.name: DivisionRing
concepts.docstring:
A DivisionRing is a Ring with multiplicative inverses for nonzero elements.
An instance of DivisionRing K includes maps ratCast : ℚ → K and qsmul : ℚ → K → K.
Those two fields are needed to implement the DivisionRing K → Algebra ℚ K instance since we need
to control the specific definitions for some special cases of K (in particular K = ℚ itself).
See also note [forgetful inheritance]. Similarly, there are maps nnratCast ℚ≥0 → K and
nnqsmul : ℚ≥0 → K → K to implement the DivisionSemiring K → Algebra ℚ≥0 K instance.
If the division ring has positive characteristic p, our division by zero convention forces
ratCast (1 / p) = 1 / 0 = 0.

concepts.name: Semifield
concepts.docstring:
A Semifield is a CommSemiring with multiplicative inverses for nonzero elements.
An instance of Semifield K includes maps nnratCast : ℚ≥0 → K and nnqsmul : ℚ≥0 → K → K.
Those two fields are needed to implement the DivisionSemiring K → Algebra ℚ≥0 K instance since we
need to control the specific definitions for some special cases of K (in particular K = ℚ≥0
itself). See also note [forgetful inheritance].
If the semifield has positive characteristic p, our division by zero convention forces
nnratCast (1 / p) = 1 / 0 = 0.

concepts.name: Field
concepts.docstring:
A Field is a CommRing with multiplicative inverses for nonzero elements.
An instance of Field K includes maps ratCast : ℚ → K and qsmul : ℚ → K → K.
Those two fields are needed to implement the DivisionRing K → Algebra ℚ K instance since we need
to control the specific definitions for some special cases of K (in particular K = ℚ itself).
See also note [forgetful inheritance].
If the field has positive characteristic p, our division by zero convention forces
ratCast (1 / p) = 1 / 0 = 0.

concepts.name: IsRightCancelMul

concepts.name: IsCancelMul

concepts.name: Semigroup

concepts.name: AddSemigroup

concepts.name: IsAddCommutative
concepts.docstring: A Prop stating that the addition is commutative.

concepts.name: IsMulCommutative

concepts.name: CommMagma

concepts.name: CommSemigroup
concepts.docstring: A commutative semigroup is a type with an associative commutative (*).

concepts.name: AddCommSemigroup
concepts.docstring: A commutative additive semigroup is a type with an associative commutative (+).

concepts.name: LeftCancelSemigroup
concepts.docstring: A LeftCancelSemigroup is a semigroup such that a * b = a * c implies b = c.

concepts.name: LibraryNote.lower_cancel_priority
concepts.docstring:
We lower the priority of inheriting from cancellative structures.
This attempts to avoid expensive checks involving bundling and unbundling with the IsDomain class.
since IsDomain already depends on Semiring, we can synthesize that one first.
Zulip discussion: https://leanprover.zulipchat.com/#narrow/stream/113488-general/topic/Why.20is.20.60simpNF.60.20complaining.20here.3F

concepts.name: AddLeftCancelSemigroup
concepts.docstring:
An AddLeftCancelSemigroup is an additive semigroup such that
a + b = a + c implies b = c.

concepts.name: RightCancelSemigroup
concepts.docstring: A RightCancelSemigroup is a semigroup such that a * b = c * b implies a = c.

concepts.name: AddRightCancelSemigroup
concepts.docstring:
An AddRightCancelSemigroup is an additive semigroup such that
a + b = c + b implies a = c.

concepts.name: AddZero
concepts.docstring:
Bundling an Add and Zero structure together without any axioms about their
compatibility. See AddZeroClass for the additional assumption that 0 is an identity.

concepts.name: MulOne
concepts.docstring:
Bundling a Mul and One structure together without any axioms about their
compatibility. See MulOneClass for the additional assumption that 1 is an identity.

concepts.name: IsDedekindFiniteAddMonoid
concepts.docstring:
An additive monoid is Dedekind-finite if every left inverse is also a right inverse.
Also called von Neumann-finite or directly finite.

concepts.name: IsDedekindFiniteMonoid
concepts.docstring:
A monoid is Dedekind-finite if every left inverse is also a right inverse.
It is more common to talk about Dedekind-finite rings, but https://arxiv.org/abs/2102.01598
does define Dedekind-finite monoids in §2.2.

concepts.name: AddZeroClass
concepts.docstring:
Typeclass for expressing that a type M with addition and a zero satisfies
0 + a = a and a + 0 = a for all a : M.

concepts.name: MulOneClass
concepts.docstring:
Typeclass for expressing that a type M with multiplication and a one satisfies
1 * a = a and a * 1 = a for all a : M.

concepts.name: LibraryNote.forgetful_inheritance
concepts.docstring:
Suppose that one can put two mathematical structures on a type, a rich one R and a poor one
P, and that one can deduce the poor structure from the rich structure through a map F (called a
forgetful functor) (think R = MetricSpace and P = TopologicalSpace). A possible
implementation would be to have a type class rich containing a field R, a type class poor
containing a field P, and an instance from rich to poor. However, this creates diamond
problems, and a better approach is to let rich extend poor and have a field saying that
F R = P.
To illustrate this, consider the pair MetricSpace / TopologicalSpace. Consider the topology
on a product of two metric spaces. With the first approach, it could be obtained by going first from
each metric space to its topology, and then taking the product topology. But it could also be
obtained by considering the product metric space (with its sup distance) and then the topology
coming from this distance. These would be the same topology, but not definitionally, which means
that from the point of view of Lean's kernel, there would be two different TopologicalSpace
instances on the product. This is not compatible with the way instances are designed and used:
there should be at most one instance of a kind on each type. This approach has created an instance
diamond that does not commute definitionally.
The second approach solves this issue. Now, a metric space contains both a distance, a topology, and
a proof that the topology coincides with the one coming from the distance. When one defines the
product of two metric spaces, one uses the sup distance and the product topology, and one has to
give the proof that the sup distance induces the product topology. Following both sides of the
instance diamond then gives rise (definitionally) to the product topology on the product space.
Another approach would be to have the rich type class take the poor type class as an instance
parameter. It would solve the diamond problem, but it would lead to a blow up of the number
of type classes one would need to declare to work with complicated classes, say a real inner
product space, and would create exponential complexity when working with products of
such complicated spaces, that are avoided by bundling things carefully as above.
Note that this description of this specific case of the product of metric spaces is oversimplified
compared to mathlib, as there is an intermediate typeclass between MetricSpace and
TopologicalSpace called UniformSpace. The above scheme is used at both levels, embedding a
topology in the uniform space structure, and a uniform structure in the metric space structure.
Note also that, when P is a proposition, there is no such issue as any two proofs of P are
definitionally equivalent in Lean.
To avoid boilerplate, there are some designs that can automatically fill the poor fields when
creating a rich structure if one doesn't want to do something special about them. For instance,
in the definition of metric spaces, default tactics fill the uniform space fields if they are
not given explicitly. One can also have a helper function creating the rich structure from a
structure with fewer fields, where the helper function fills the remaining fields. See for instance
UniformSpace.ofCore or RealInnerProduct.ofCore.
For more details on this question, called the forgetful inheritance pattern, see Competing
inheritance paths in dependent type theory: a case study in functional
analysis.

concepts.name: npowBinRecAuto
concepts.docstring:
An abbreviation for npowBinRec with an additional typeclass assumption on associativity

concepts.name: nsmulBinRecAuto
concepts.docstring:
An abbreviation for nsmulBinRec with an additional typeclass assumption on associativity

concepts.name: AddMonoid
concepts.docstring: An AddMonoid is an AddSemigroup with an element 0 such that 0 + a = a + 0 = a.

concepts.name: Monoid
concepts.docstring: A Monoid is a Semigroup with an element 1 such that 1 * a = a * 1 = a.

concepts.name: IsAddTorsionFree
concepts.docstring:
An additive monoid is torsion-free if scalar multiplication by every non-zero element n : ℕ is
injective.

concepts.name: IsMulTorsionFree
concepts.docstring: A monoid is torsion-free if power by every non-zero element n : ℕ is injective.

concepts.name: AddCommMonoid
concepts.docstring: An additive commutative monoid is an additive monoid with commutative (+).

concepts.name: CommMonoid
concepts.docstring: A commutative monoid is a monoid with commutative (*).

concepts.name: AddLeftCancelMonoid
concepts.docstring:
An additive monoid in which addition is left-cancellative.
Main examples are ℕ and groups. This is the right typeclass for many sum lemmas, as having a zero
is useful to define the sum over the empty set, so AddLeftCancelSemigroup is not enough.

concepts.name: LeftCancelMonoid
concepts.docstring: A monoid in which multiplication is left-cancellative.

concepts.name: AddRightCancelMonoid
concepts.docstring:
An additive monoid in which addition is right-cancellative.
Main examples are ℕ and groups. This is the right typeclass for many sum lemmas, as having a zero
is useful to define the sum over the empty set, so AddRightCancelSemigroup is not enough.

concepts.name: RightCancelMonoid
concepts.docstring: A monoid in which multiplication is right-cancellative.

concepts.name: AddCancelMonoid
concepts.docstring:
An additive monoid in which addition is cancellative on both sides.
Main examples are ℕ and groups. This is the right typeclass for many sum lemmas, as having a zero
is useful to define the sum over the empty set, so AddRightCancelMonoid is not enough.

concepts.name: CancelMonoid
concepts.docstring: A monoid in which multiplication is cancellative.

concepts.name: AddCancelCommMonoid
concepts.docstring: Commutative version of AddCancelMonoid.

concepts.name: CancelCommMonoid
concepts.docstring: Commutative version of CancelMonoid.

concepts.name: zpowRec
concepts.docstring:
The fundamental power operation in a group. zpowRec n a = a*a*...*a n times, for integer n.
Use instead a ^ n, which has better definitional behavior.

concepts.name: zsmulRec
concepts.docstring:
The fundamental scalar multiplication in an additive group. zpowRec n a = a+a+...+a n
times, for integer n. Use instead n • a, which has better definitional behavior.

concepts.name: InvolutiveNeg
concepts.docstring: Auxiliary typeclass for types with an involutive Neg.

concepts.name: InvolutiveInv
concepts.docstring: Auxiliary typeclass for types with an involutive Inv.

concepts.name: DivInvMonoid.div'
concepts.docstring:
In a class equipped with instances of both Monoid and Inv, this definition records what the
default definition for Div would be: a * b⁻¹.  This is later provided as the default value for
the Div instance in DivInvMonoid.
We keep it as a separate definition rather than inlining it in DivInvMonoid so that the Div
field of individual DivInvMonoids constructed using that default value will not be unfolded at
.instance transparency.

concepts.name: DivInvMonoid
concepts.docstring:
A DivInvMonoid is a Monoid with operations / and ⁻¹ satisfying
div_eq_mul_inv : ∀ a b, a / b = a * b⁻¹.
This deduplicates the name div_eq_mul_inv.
The default for div is such that a / b = a * b⁻¹ holds by definition.
Adding div as a field rather than defining a / b := a * b⁻¹ allows us to
avoid certain classes of unification failures, for example:
Let Foo X be a type with a ∀ X, Div (Foo X) instance but no
∀ X, Inv (Foo X), e.g. when Foo X is a EuclideanDomain. Suppose we
also have an instance ∀ X [Cromulent X], GroupWithZero (Foo X). Then the
(/) coming from GroupWithZero.div cannot be definitionally equal to
the (/) coming from Foo.Div.
In the same way, adding a zpow field makes it possible to avoid definitional failures
in diamonds. See the definition of Monoid and Note [forgetful inheritance] for more
explanations on this.

concepts.name: SubNegMonoid.sub'
concepts.docstring:
In a class equipped with instances of both AddMonoid and Neg, this definition records what
the default definition for Sub would be: a + -b.  This is later provided as the default value
for the Sub instance in SubNegMonoid.
We keep it as a separate definition rather than inlining it in SubNegMonoid so that the Sub
field of individual SubNegMonoids constructed using that default value will not be unfolded at
.instance transparency.

concepts.name: SubNegMonoid
concepts.docstring:
A SubNegMonoid is an AddMonoid with unary - and binary - operations
satisfying sub_eq_add_neg : ∀ a b, a - b = a + -b.
The default for sub is such that a - b = a + -b holds by definition.
Adding sub as a field rather than defining a - b := a + -b allows us to
avoid certain classes of unification failures, for example:
Let foo X be a type with a ∀ X, Sub (Foo X) instance but no
∀ X, Neg (Foo X). Suppose we also have an instance
∀ X [Cromulent X], AddGroup (Foo X). Then the (-) coming from
AddGroup.sub cannot be definitionally equal to the (-) coming from
Foo.Sub.
In the same way, adding a zsmul field makes it possible to avoid definitional failures
in diamonds. See the definition of AddMonoid and Note [forgetful inheritance] for more
explanations on this.

concepts.name: IsAddCyclic
concepts.docstring: A group is called cyclic if it is generated by a single element.

concepts.name: IsCyclic
concepts.docstring: A group is called cyclic if it is generated by a single element.

concepts.name: NegZeroClass
concepts.docstring: Typeclass for expressing that -0 = 0.

concepts.name: SubNegZeroMonoid
concepts.docstring: A SubNegMonoid where -0 = 0.

concepts.name: InvOneClass
concepts.docstring: Typeclass for expressing that 1⁻¹ = 1.

concepts.name: DivInvOneMonoid
concepts.docstring: A DivInvMonoid where 1⁻¹ = 1.

concepts.name: SubtractionMonoid
concepts.docstring:
A SubtractionMonoid is a SubNegMonoid with involutive negation and such that
-(a + b) = -b + -a and a + b = 0 → -a = b.

concepts.name: DivisionMonoid
concepts.docstring:
A DivisionMonoid is a DivInvMonoid with involutive inversion and such that
(a * b)⁻¹ = b⁻¹ * a⁻¹ and a * b = 1 → a⁻¹ = b.
This is the immediate common ancestor of Group and GroupWithZero.

concepts.name: SubtractionCommMonoid
concepts.docstring: Commutative SubtractionMonoid.

concepts.name: DivisionCommMonoid
concepts.docstring:
Commutative DivisionMonoid.
This is the immediate common ancestor of CommGroup and CommGroupWithZero.

concepts.name: Group
concepts.docstring:
A Group is a Monoid with an operation ⁻¹ satisfying a⁻¹ * a = 1.
There is also a division operation / such that a / b = a * b⁻¹,
with a default so that a / b = a * b⁻¹ holds by definition.
Use Group.ofLeftAxioms or Group.ofRightAxioms to define a group structure
on a type with the minimum proof obligations.

concepts.name: AddGroup
concepts.docstring:
An AddGroup is an AddMonoid with a unary - satisfying -a + a = 0.
There is also a binary operation - such that a - b = a + -b,
with a default so that a - b = a + -b holds by definition.
Use AddGroup.ofLeftAxioms or AddGroup.ofRightAxioms to define an
additive group structure on a type with the minimum proof obligations.

concepts.name: AddCommGroup
concepts.docstring: An additive commutative group is an additive group with commutative (+).

concepts.name: CommGroup
concepts.docstring: A commutative group is a group with commutative (*).

concepts.name: IsMulCommutative.instCommMagma
concepts.docstring:

This is primarily used to deduce the bundled version from the unbundled one for commutative
subobjects in a noncommutative ambient type. As such this is only available inside the
IsMulCommutative scope so as to avoid deleterious effects to type class synthesis for bundled
commutativity.
See note [commutative subobjects].

concepts.name: Distrib

A typeclass stating that multiplication is left and right distributive
over addition.

concepts.name: LeftDistribClass

concepts.name: RightDistribClass
concepts.docstring: A typeclass stating that multiplication is right distributive over addition.

concepts.name: NonUnitalNonAssocSemiring
concepts.docstring:
A not-necessarily-unital, not-necessarily-associative semiring. See CommutatorRing and the
documentation thereof in case you need a NonUnitalNonAssocSemiring instance on a Lie ring
or a Lie algebra.

concepts.name: NonUnitalSemiring
concepts.docstring: An associative but not-necessarily unital semiring.

concepts.name: NonAssocSemiring
concepts.docstring: A unital but not-necessarily-associative semiring.

concepts.name: NonUnitalNonAssocRing
concepts.docstring: A not-necessarily-unital, not-necessarily-associative ring.

concepts.name: NonUnitalRing

concepts.name: NonAssocRing

concepts.name: Semiring
concepts.docstring:
A Semiring is a type with addition, multiplication, a 0 and a 1 where addition is
commutative and associative, multiplication is associative and left and right distributive over
addition, and 0 and 1 are additive and multiplicative identities.

concepts.name: Ring
concepts.docstring: A Ring is a Semiring with negation making it an additive group.

concepts.name: NonUnitalNonAssocCommSemiring
concepts.docstring: A not-necessarily-unital, not-necessarily-associative, but commutative semiring.

concepts.name: NonUnitalCommSemiring
concepts.docstring:
A non-unital commutative semiring is a NonUnitalSemiring with commutative multiplication.
In other words, it is a type with the following structures: additive commutative monoid
(AddCommMonoid), commutative semigroup (CommSemigroup), distributive laws (Distrib), and
multiplication by zero law (MulZeroClass).

concepts.name: NonAssocCommSemiring
concepts.docstring:
A non-associative commutative semiring is a NonAssocSemiring with commutative
multiplication.

concepts.name: CommSemiring
concepts.docstring: A commutative semiring is a semiring with commutative multiplication.

concepts.name: HasDistribNeg
concepts.docstring:
Typeclass for a negation operator that distributes across multiplication.
This is useful for dealing with submonoids of a ring that contain -1 without having to duplicate
lemmas.

concepts.name: NonUnitalNonAssocCommRing
concepts.docstring:
A non-unital non-associative commutative ring is a NonUnitalNonAssocRing with commutative
multiplication.

concepts.name: NonUnitalCommRing
concepts.docstring: A non-unital commutative ring is a NonUnitalRing with commutative multiplication.

concepts.name: NonAssocCommRing
concepts.docstring: A non-associative commutative ring is a NonAssocRing with commutative multiplication.

concepts.name: CommRing
concepts.docstring: A commutative ring is a ring with commutative multiplication.

concepts.name: IsDomain
concepts.docstring:
A domain is a nontrivial semiring such that multiplication by a nonzero element
is cancellative on both sides. In other words, a nontrivial semiring R satisfying
∀ {a b c : R}, a ≠ 0 → a * b = a * c → b = c and
∀ {a b c : R}, b ≠ 0 → a * b = c * b → a = c.
This is implemented as a mixin for Semiring α.
To obtain an integral domain use [CommRing α] [IsDomain α].

concepts.name: IsMulCommutative.instNonUnitalNonAssocCommSemiring
concepts.docstring:

This is primarily used to deduce the bundled version from the unbundled one for commutative

Reorder an average.
The difference with Finset.expect_nbij' is that the bijection is specified as a surjective
injection, rather than by an inverse function.
The difference with Finset.expect_bij is that the bijection is a non-dependent function, rather
than being allowed to use membership of the domain of the average.

theorems.name: Finset.expect_nbij'
theorems.type_signature: (s.expect fun (i : ι) => f i) = t.expect fun (i : κ) => g i
theorems.docstring:
Reorder an average.
The difference with Finset.expect_nbij is that the bijection is specified with an inverse, rather
than as a surjective injection.
The difference with Finset.expect_bij' is that the bijection and its inverse are non-dependent
functions, rather than being allowed to use membership of the domains of the averages.
The difference with Finset.expect_equiv is that bijectivity is only required to hold on the
domains of the averages, rather than on the entire types.

theorems.name: Fin.prod_prod_eq_prod_triangle_mul
theorems.type_signature: ∏ i : Fin (n + 1), ∏ j : Fin n, f i j = ∏ i : Fin n, ∏ j ∈ Finset.Ici i, f i.castSucc j * f j.succ i
theorems.docstring:
The product of g i j over i j : Fin (n + 1), i ≠ j,
is equal to the product of g i j * g j i over i < j.
The additive version of this lemma is useful for some proofs about differential forms.
In this application, the function has the signature f : Fin (n + 1) → Fin n → M,
where f i j means g i (Fin.succAbove i j) in the informal statements.
Similarly, the product of g i j * g j i over i < j
is written as f (Fin.castSucc i) j * f (Fin.succ j) i over i j : Fin n, j ≥ i.

theorems.name: Fin.sum_sum_eq_sum_triangle_add

theorems.docstring:
The sum of g i j over i j : Fin (n + 1), i ≠ j,
is equal to the sum of g i j + g j i over i < j.
This lemma is useful for some proofs about differential forms.
In this application, the function has the signature f : Fin (n + 1) → Fin n → M,
where f i j means g i (Fin.succAbove i j) in the informal statements.
Similarly, the sum of g i j + g j i over i < j
is written as f (Fin.castSucc i) j + f (Fin.succ j) i over i j : Fin n, j ≥ i.

theorems.name: Fin.inv_partialProd_mul_eq_contractNth
theorems.type_signature: (partialProd g (j.succ.succAbove k.castSucc))⁻¹ * partialProd g (j.succAbove k).succ = j.contractNth (fun (x1 x2 : G) => x1 * x2) g k
theorems.docstring:
Let (g₀, g₁, ..., gₙ) be a tuple of elements in Gⁿ⁺¹.
Then if k < j, this says (g₀g₁...gₖ₋₁)⁻¹ * g₀g₁...gₖ = gₖ.
If k = j, it says (g₀g₁...gₖ₋₁)⁻¹ * g₀g₁...gₖ₊₁ = gₖgₖ₊₁.
If k > j, it says (g₀g₁...gₖ)⁻¹ * g₀g₁...gₖ₊₁ = gₖ₊₁.
Useful for defining group cohomology.

theorems.name: Fin.neg_partialSum_add_eq_contractNth
theorems.type_signature: -partialSum g (j.succ.succAbove k.castSucc) + partialSum g (j.succAbove k).succ = j.contractNth (fun (x1 x2 : G) => x1 + x2) g k
theorems.docstring:
Let (g₀, g₁, ..., gₙ) be a tuple of elements in Gⁿ⁺¹.
Then if k < j, this says -(g₀ + g₁ + ... + gₖ₋₁) + (g₀ + g₁ + ... + gₖ) = gₖ.
If k = j, it says -(g₀ + g₁ + ... + gₖ₋₁) + (g₀ + g₁ + ... + gₖ₊₁) = gₖ + gₖ₊₁.
If k > j, it says -(g₀ + g₁ + ... + gₖ) + (g₀ + g₁ + ... + gₖ₊₁) = gₖ₊₁.
Useful for defining group cohomology.

theorems.name: finprod_mul_distrib
theorems.type_signature: ∏ᶠ (i : α), f i * g i = (∏ᶠ (i : α), f i) * ∏ᶠ (i : α), g i
theorems.docstring:
If the multiplicative supports of f and g are finite, then the product of f i * g i equals
the product of f i multiplied by the product of g i.

theorems.name: finsum_add_distrib
theorems.type_signature: ∑ᶠ (i : α), (f i + g i) = ∑ᶠ (i : α), f i + ∑ᶠ (i : α), g i
theorems.docstring:
If the additive supports of f and g are finite, then the sum of f i + g i
equals the sum of f i plus the sum of g i.

theorems.name: finprod_div_distrib
theorems.type_signature: ∏ᶠ (i : α), f i / g i = (∏ᶠ (i : α), f i) / ∏ᶠ (i : α), g i
theorems.docstring:
If the multiplicative supports of f and g are finite, then the product of f i / g i
equals the product of f i divided by the product of g i.

theorems.name: finsum_sub_distrib
theorems.type_signature: ∑ᶠ (i : α), (f i - g i) = ∑ᶠ (i : α), f i - ∑ᶠ (i : α), g i
theorems.docstring:
If the additive supports of f and g are finite, then the sum of f i - g i
equals the sum of f i minus the sum of g i.

theorems.name: finprod_mem_mul_distrib'
theorems.docstring:
A more general version of finprod_mem_mul_distrib that only requires s ∩ mulSupport f and
s ∩ mulSupport g rather than s to be finite.

theorems.name: finsum_mem_add_distrib'
theorems.docstring:

and s ∩ support g rather than s to be finite.

theorems.name: finprod_mem_one
theorems.docstring: The product of the constant function 1 over any set equals 1.

theorems.name: finsum_mem_zero
theorems.docstring: The sum of the constant function 0 over any set equals 0.

theorems.name: finprod_mem_of_eqOn_one
theorems.docstring: If a function f equals 1 on a set s, then the product of f i over i ∈ s equals 1.

theorems.name: finsum_mem_of_eqOn_zero
theorems.docstring:
If a function f equals 0 on a set s, then the sum of f i over i ∈ s
equals 0.

theorems.name: exists_ne_one_of_finprod_mem_ne_one
theorems.docstring:
If the product of f i over i ∈ s is not equal to 1, then there is some x ∈ s such that
f x ≠ 1.

theorems.name: exists_ne_zero_of_finsum_mem_ne_zero
theorems.docstring:
If the sum of f i over i ∈ s is not equal to 0, then there is some x ∈ s
such that f x ≠ 0.

theorems.name: finprod_mem_mul_distrib
theorems.docstring:
Given a finite set s, the product of f i * g i over i ∈ s equals the product of f i
over i ∈ s times the product of g i over i ∈ s.

theorems.name: finsum_mem_add_distrib
theorems.docstring:
Given a finite set s, the sum of f i + g i over i ∈ s equals the sum of f i
over i ∈ s plus the sum of g i over i ∈ s.

theorems.name: MonoidHom.map_finprod_mem
theorems.docstring:
Given a monoid homomorphism g : M →* N and a function f : α → M, the value of g at the
product of f i over i ∈ s equals the product of g (f i) over s.

theorems.name: AddMonoidHom.map_finsum_mem
theorems.docstring:
Given an additive monoid homomorphism g : M →* N and a function f : α → M, the
value of g at the sum of f i over i ∈ s equals the sum of g (f i) over s.

theorems.name: finprod_mem_div_distrib
theorems.docstring:
Given a finite set s, the product of f i / g i over i ∈ s equals the product of f i
over i ∈ s divided by the product of g i over i ∈ s.

theorems.name: finsum_mem_sub_distrib
theorems.docstring:
Given a finite set s, the sum of f i / g i over i ∈ s equals the sum of f i
over i ∈ s minus the sum of g i over i ∈ s.

theorems.name: finprod_mem_empty
theorems.docstring: The product of any function over an empty set is 1.

theorems.name: finsum_mem_empty
theorems.docstring: The sum of any function over an empty set is 0.

theorems.name: nonempty_of_finprod_mem_ne_one

theorems.name: nonempty_of_finsum_mem_ne_zero
theorems.docstring: A set s is nonempty if the sum of some function over s is not equal to 0.

theorems.name: finprod_mem_union_inter
theorems.docstring:
Given finite sets s and t, the product of f i over i ∈ s ∪ t times the product of
f i over i ∈ s ∩ t equals the product of f i over i ∈ s times the product of f i
over i ∈ t.

theorems.docstring:
Given finite sets s and t, the sum of f i over i ∈ s ∪ t plus the sum of
f i over i ∈ s ∩ t equals the sum of f i over i ∈ s plus the sum of f i
over i ∈ t.

theorems.docstring:

times the product of f i over t \ s equals the product of f i over i ∈ t.

then its product over f : α →₀ M is the same as multiplying the value on any element
y : α by the product over erase y f.

y : α to the sum over erase y f.
