theorems.name: Finsupp.prod_ne_zero_iff
theorems.type_signature: f.prod g ≠ 0 ↔ ∀ i ∈ f.support, g i (f i) ≠ 0

theorems.name: map_finsuppProd
theorems.type_signature: h (f.prod g) = f.prod fun (a : α) (b : M) => h (g a b)

theorems.name: map_finsuppSum
theorems.type_signature: h (f.sum g) = f.sum fun (a : α) (b : M) => h (g a b)

theorems.name: MonoidHom.coe_finsuppProd
theorems.type_signature: ⇑(f.prod g) = f.prod fun (i : α) (fi : β) => ⇑(g i fi)

theorems.name: AddMonoidHom.coe_finsuppSum
theorems.type_signature: ⇑(f.sum g) = f.sum fun (i : α) (fi : β) => ⇑(g i fi)

theorems.name: MonoidHom.finsuppProd_apply
theorems.type_signature: (f.prod g) x = f.prod fun (i : α) (fi : β) => (g i fi) x

theorems.name: AddMonoidHom.finsuppSum_apply
theorems.type_signature: (f.sum g) x = f.sum fun (i : α) (fi : β) => (g i fi) x

theorems.name: Finsupp.single_finsetSum
theorems.type_signature: single a (∑ b ∈ s, f b) = ∑ b ∈ s, single a (f b)

theorems.name: Finsupp.single_finset_sum
theorems.type_signature: single a (∑ b ∈ s, f b) = ∑ b ∈ s, single a (f b)
theorems.docstring: Alias of Finsupp.single_finsetSum.

theorems.name: Finsupp.single_sum
theorems.type_signature: single a (s.sum f) = s.sum fun (d : ι) (c : M) => single a (f d c)

theorems.name: Finsupp.prod_neg_index
theorems.type_signature: (-g).prod h = g.prod fun (a : α) (b : G) => h a (-b)

theorems.name: Finsupp.sum_neg_index
theorems.type_signature: (-g).sum h = g.sum fun (a : α) (b : G) => h a (-b)

theorems.name: Finsupp.finsetSum_apply
theorems.type_signature: (∑ i ∈ S, f i) a = ∑ i ∈ S, (f i) a

theorems.name: Finsupp.finset_sum_apply
theorems.type_signature: (∑ i ∈ S, f i) a = ∑ i ∈ S, (f i) a
theorems.docstring: Alias of Finsupp.finsetSum_apply.

theorems.name: Finsupp.sum_apply
theorems.type_signature: (f.sum g) a₂ = f.sum fun (a₁ : α) (b : M) => (g a₁ b) a₂

theorems.name: Finsupp.coe_finset_sum
theorems.docstring: Alias of Finsupp.coe_finsetSum.

theorems.name: Finsupp.coe_sum
theorems.type_signature: ⇑(f.sum g) = f.sum fun (a₁ : α) (b : M) => ⇑(g a₁ b)

theorems.name: Finsupp.support_sum
theorems.type_signature: (f.sum g).support ⊆ f.support.biUnion fun (a : α) => (g a (f a)).support

theorems.name: Finsupp.support_finset_sum
theorems.docstring: Alias of Finsupp.support_finsetSum.

theorems.name: Finsupp.sum_eq_one_iff
theorems.type_signature: (d.sum fun (x : α) (n : ℕ) => n) = 1 ↔ ∃ (a : α), d = single a 1

theorems.name: Finsupp.prod_mul
theorems.type_signature: (f.prod fun (a : α) (b : M) => h₁ a b * h₂ a b) = f.prod h₁ * f.prod h₂

theorems.name: Finsupp.sum_add
theorems.type_signature: (f.sum fun (a : α) (b : M) => h₁ a b + h₂ a b) = f.sum h₁ + f.sum h₂

theorems.name: Finsupp.prod_inv
theorems.type_signature: (f.prod fun (a : α) (b : M) => (h a b)⁻¹) = (f.prod h)⁻¹

theorems.name: Finsupp.sum_neg
theorems.type_signature: (f.sum fun (a : α) (b : M) => -h a b) = -f.sum h

theorems.name: Finsupp.sum_sub
theorems.type_signature: (f.sum fun (a : α) (b : M) => h₁ a b - h₂ a b) = f.sum h₁ - f.sum h₂

theorems.name: Finsupp.prod_add_index
theorems.type_signature: (f + g).prod h = f.prod h * g.prod h
theorems.docstring:
Taking the product under h is an additive-to-multiplicative homomorphism of finsupps,
if h is an additive-to-multiplicative homomorphism on the support.
This is a more general version of Finsupp.prod_add_index'; the latter has simpler hypotheses.

theorems.name: Finsupp.sum_add_index
theorems.type_signature: (f + g).sum h = f.sum h + g.sum h
theorems.docstring:
Taking the product under h is an additive homomorphism of finsupps, if h is an
additive homomorphism on the support. This is a more general version of
Finsupp.sum_add_index'; the latter has simpler hypotheses.

theorems.name: Finsupp.prod_add_index'
theorems.type_signature: (f + g).prod h = f.prod h * g.prod h
theorems.docstring:
Taking the product under h is an additive-to-multiplicative homomorphism of finsupps,
if h is an additive-to-multiplicative homomorphism.
This is a more specialized version of Finsupp.prod_add_index with simpler hypotheses.

theorems.name: Finsupp.sum_add_index'
theorems.type_signature: (f + g).sum h = f.sum h + g.sum h
theorems.docstring:
Taking the sum under h is an additive homomorphism of finsupps,if h is an additive
homomorphism. This is a more specific version of Finsupp.sum_add_index with simpler
hypotheses.

theorems.name: Finsupp.sum_hom_add_index
theorems.type_signature: ((f + g).sum fun (x : α) => ⇑(h x)) = (f.sum fun (x : α) => ⇑(h x)) + g.sum fun (x : α) => ⇑(h x)

theorems.name: Finsupp.prod_hom_add_index
theorems.type_signature: ((f + g).prod fun (a : α) (b : M) => (h a) (Multiplicative.ofAdd b)) = (f.prod fun (a : α) (b : M) => (h a) (Multiplicative.ofAdd b)) * g.prod fun (a : α) (b : M) => (h a) (Multiplicative.ofAdd b)

theorems.name: Finsupp.liftAddHom_apply
theorems.type_signature: (liftAddHom F) f = f.sum fun (x : α) => ⇑(F x)

theorems.name: Finsupp.liftAddHom_symm_apply_apply
theorems.type_signature: (liftAddHom.symm F x) y = F (single x y)

theorems.name: Finsupp.univ_sum_single
theorems.type_signature: ∑ a : α, single a (f a) = f
theorems.docstring: The Finsupp version of Finset.univ_sum_single

theorems.name: Finsupp.univ_sum_single_apply
theorems.type_signature: ∑ j : α, (single i m) j = m

theorems.name: Finsupp.univ_sum_single_apply'
theorems.type_signature: ∑ j : α, (single j m) i = m

theorems.name: Finsupp.sum_single_add_single
theorems.type_signature: (single f₁ g₁ + single f₂ g₂).sum F = F f₁ g₁ + F f₂ g₂

theorems.name: Finsupp.equivFunOnFinite_symm_eq_sum
theorems.type_signature: equivFunOnFinite.symm f = ∑ a : α, single a (f a)

theorems.name: Finsupp.coe_univ_sum_single
theorems.type_signature: ⇑(∑ a : α, single a (f a)) = f

theorems.name: Finsupp.equivFunOnFinite_symm_sum
theorems.type_signature: ((equivFunOnFinite.symm f).sum fun (x : α) (n : M) => n) = ∑ a : α, f a

theorems.name: Finsupp.comp_liftAddHom
theorems.type_signature: g.comp (liftAddHom f) = liftAddHom fun (a : α) => g.comp (f a)

theorems.name: Finsupp.sum_sub_index
theorems.type_signature: (f - g).sum h = f.sum h - g.sum h

theorems.name: Finsupp.prod_embDomain
theorems.type_signature: (embDomain f v).prod g = v.prod fun (a : α) (b : M) => g (f a) b

theorems.name: Finsupp.sum_embDomain
theorems.type_signature: (embDomain f v).sum g = v.sum fun (a : α) (b : M) => g (f a) b

theorems.name: Finsupp.prod_finsetSum_index
theorems.type_signature: ∏ i ∈ s, (g i).prod h = (∑ i ∈ s, g i).prod h

theorems.name: Finsupp.sum_finsetSum_index
theorems.type_signature: ∑ i ∈ s, (g i).sum h = (∑ i ∈ s, g i).sum h

theorems.name: Finsupp.sum_finset_sum_index
theorems.type_signature: ∑ i ∈ s, (g i).sum h = (∑ i ∈ s, g i).sum h
theorems.docstring: Alias of Finsupp.sum_finsetSum_index.

theorems.name: Finsupp.prod_finset_sum_index
theorems.type_signature: ∏ i ∈ s, (g i).prod h = (∑ i ∈ s, g i).prod h
theorems.docstring: Alias of Finsupp.prod_finsetSum_index.

theorems.name: Finsupp.prod_sum_index
theorems.type_signature: (f.sum g).prod h = f.prod fun (a : α) (b : M) => (g a b).prod h

theorems.name: Finsupp.sum_sum_index
theorems.type_signature: (f.sum g).sum h = f.sum fun (a : α) (b : M) => (g a b).sum h

theorems.name: Finsupp.multiset_sum_sum_index
theorems.type_signature: f.sum.sum h = (Multiset.map (fun (g : α →₀ M) => g.sum h) f).sum

theorems.name: Finsupp.support_sum_eq_biUnion
theorems.type_signature: (∑ i ∈ s, g i).support = s.biUnion fun (i : ι) => (g i).support

theorems.name: Finsupp.multiset_map_sum
theorems.type_signature: Multiset.map m (f.sum h) = f.sum fun (a : α) (b : M) => Multiset.map m (h a b)

theorems.name: Finsupp.multiset_sum_sum
theorems.type_signature: (f.sum h).sum = f.sum fun (a : α) (b : M) => (h a b).sum

theorems.name: Finsupp.prod_add_index_of_disjoint
theorems.type_signature: (f1 + f2).prod g = f1.prod g * f2.prod g
theorems.docstring:
For disjoint f1 and f2, and function g, the product of the products of g
over f1 and f2 equals the product of g over f1 + f2

theorems.name: Finsupp.sum_add_index_of_disjoint
theorems.type_signature: (f1 + f2).sum g = f1.sum g + f2.sum g
theorems.docstring:
For disjoint f1 and f2, and function g, the sum of the sums of g
over f1 and f2 equals the sum of g over f1 + f2

theorems.name: Finsupp.indicator_eq_sum_attach_single
theorems.type_signature: indicator s f = ∑ x ∈ s.attach, single (↑x) (f ↑x ⋯)

theorems.name: Finsupp.indicator_eq_sum_single
theorems.type_signature: (indicator s fun (x : α) (x_1 : x ∈ s) => f x) = ∑ x ∈ s, single x (f x)

theorems.name: Finsupp.prod_indicator_index_eq_prod_attach
theorems.type_signature: (indicator s f).prod h = ∏ x ∈ s.attach, h (↑x) (f ↑x ⋯)

theorems.name: Finsupp.sum_indicator_index_eq_sum_attach
theorems.type_signature: (indicator s f).sum h = ∑ x ∈ s.attach, h (↑x) (f ↑x ⋯)

theorems.name: Finsupp.prod_attach_index
theorems.type_signature: ∏ x ∈ s.attach, h (↑x) (f ↑x) = ∏ x ∈ s, h x (f x)

theorems.name: Finsupp.sum_attach_index
theorems.type_signature: ∑ x ∈ s.attach, h (↑x) (f ↑x) = ∑ x ∈ s, h x (f x)

theorems.name: Finsupp.prod_indicator_index
theorems.type_signature: (indicator s fun (x : α) (x_1 : x ∈ s) => f x).prod h = ∏ x ∈ s, h x (f x)

theorems.name: Finsupp.sum_indicator_index
theorems.type_signature: (indicator s fun (x : α) (x_1 : x ∈ s) => f x).sum h = ∑ x ∈ s, h x (f x)

theorems.name: Finsupp.prod_mul_eq_prod_mul_of_exists
theorems.type_signature: f.prod g * n₁ = f.prod g * n₂

theorems.name: Finsupp.sum_add_eq_sum_add_of_exists
theorems.type_signature: f.sum g + n₁ = f.sum g + n₂

theorems.name: Finset.sum_apply'
theorems.type_signature: (∑ k ∈ s, f k) i = ∑ k ∈ s, (f k) i

theorems.name: Finsupp.sum_apply'
theorems.type_signature: g.sum k x = g.sum fun (i : ι) (b : A) => k i b x

theorems.name: Finsupp.sum_apply''
theorems.type_signature: (g.sum k) x = g.sum fun (i : ι) (a : A) => (k i a) x
theorems.docstring:
Version of Finsupp.sum_apply' that applies in large generality to linear combinations
of functions in any FunLike type on which addition is defined pointwise.
At the time of writing Mathlib does not have a typeclass to express the condition
that addition on a FunLike type is pointwise; hence this is asserted via explicit hypotheses.

theorems.name: Finsupp.sum_mul
theorems.type_signature: s.sum f * b = s.sum fun (a : α) (c : R) => f a c * b

theorems.name: Finsupp.mul_sum
theorems.type_signature: b * s.sum f = s.sum fun (a : α) (c : R) => b * f a c

theorems.name: Multiset.card_finsuppSum
theorems.type_signature: (f.sum g).card = f.sum fun (i : ι) (m : M) => (g i m).card

theorems.name: Nat.prod_pow_pos_of_zero_notMem_support
theorems.type_signature: 0 < f.prod fun (x1 x2 : ℕ) => x1 ^ x2
theorems.docstring: If 0 : ℕ is not in the support of f : ℕ →₀ ℕ then 0 < ∏ x ∈ f.support, x ^ (f x).

theorems.name: MulOpposite.op_finsuppSum
theorems.type_signature: op (f.sum g) = f.sum fun (i : ι) (n : N) => op (g i n)

theorems.name: MulOpposite.unop_finsuppSum
theorems.type_signature: unop (f.sum g) = f.sum fun (i : ι) (n : N) => unop (g i n)

theorems.name: AddOpposite.op_finsuppProd
theorems.type_signature: op (f.prod g) = f.prod fun (i : ι) (n : N) => op (g i n)

theorems.name: AddOpposite.unop_finsuppProd
theorems.type_signature: unop (f.prod g) = f.prod fun (i : ι) (n : N) => unop (g i n)

theorems.name: Finsupp.sum_cons
theorems.type_signature: ((cons i σ).sum fun (x : Fin (n + 1)) (e : M) => e) = i + σ.sum fun (x : Fin n) (e : M) => e

theorems.name: Finsupp.sum_cons'
theorems.type_signature: (cons i σ).sum f = f 0 i + σ.sum (Fin.tail f)

theorems.name: finTwoArrowEquiv'_sum_eq
theorems.type_signature: (((finTwoArrowEquiv' M).symm d).sum fun (x : Fin 2) (n : M) => n) = d.1 + d.2

theorems.name: Finset.prod_eq_fold
theorems.type_signature: ∏ i ∈ s, f i = fold (fun (x1 x2 : M) => x1 * x2) 1 f s

theorems.name: Finset.sum_eq_fold
theorems.type_signature: ∑ i ∈ s, f i = fold (fun (x1 x2 : M) => x1 + x2) 0 f s

theorems.name: Finset.prod_cons
theorems.type_signature: ∏ x ∈ cons a s h, f x = f a * ∏ x ∈ s, f x

theorems.name: Finset.sum_cons
theorems.type_signature: ∑ x ∈ cons a s h, f x = f a + ∑ x ∈ s, f x

theorems.name: Finset.prod_cons'
theorems.type_signature: (cons a s h).prod = fun (f : ι → M) => f a * ∏ x ∈ s, f x
theorems.docstring: Variant of prod_cons not applied to a function.

theorems.name: Finset.sum_cons'
theorems.type_signature: (cons a s h).sum = fun (f : ι → M) => f a + ∑ x ∈ s, f x

theorems.name: Finset.prod_insert
theorems.type_signature: a ∉ s → ∏ x ∈ insert a s, f x = f a * ∏ x ∈ s, f x

theorems.name: Finset.sum_insert
theorems.type_signature: a ∉ s → ∑ x ∈ insert a s, f x = f a + ∑ x ∈ s, f x

theorems.name: Finset.prod_insert'
theorems.type_signature: (insert a s).prod = fun (f : ι → M) => f a * ∏ x ∈ s, f x
theorems.docstring: Variant of prod_insert not applied to a function.

theorems.name: Finset.sum_insert'
theorems.type_signature: (insert a s).sum = fun (f : ι → M) => f a + ∑ x ∈ s, f x

theorems.name: Finset.prod_insert_of_eq_one_if_notMem
theorems.type_signature: ∏ x ∈ insert a s, f x = ∏ x ∈ s, f x
theorems.docstring:
The product of f over insert a s is the same as
the product over s, as long as a is in s or f a = 1.

theorems.name: Finset.sum_insert_of_eq_zero_if_notMem
theorems.type_signature: ∑ x ∈ insert a s, f x = ∑ x ∈ s, f x
theorems.docstring:
The sum of f over insert a s is the same as
the sum over s, as long as a is in s or f a = 0.

theorems.name: Finset.prod_insert_one
theorems.type_signature: ∏ x ∈ insert a s, f x = ∏ x ∈ s, f x
theorems.docstring:
The product of f over insert a s is the same as
the product over s, as long as f a = 1.

theorems.name: Finset.sum_insert_zero
theorems.type_signature: ∑ x ∈ insert a s, f x = ∑ x ∈ s, f x
theorems.docstring:
The sum of f over insert a s is the same as
the sum over s, as long as f a = 0.

theorems.name: Finset.prod_singleton'
theorems.docstring: Variant of prod_singleton not applied to a function.

theorems.name: Finset.prod_pair
theorems.type_signature: ∏ x ∈ {a, b}, f x = f a * f b

theorems.name: Finset.sum_pair
theorems.type_signature: ∑ x ∈ {a, b}, f x = f a + f b

theorems.name: Finset.prod_image
theorems.type_signature: Set.InjOn g ↑s → ∏ x ∈ image g s, f x = ∏ x ∈ s, f (g x)
theorems.docstring:
If a function is injective on a finset, products over the original finset or its image coincide.
See also prod_image_of_pairwise_eq_one for a version with weaker assumptions.

theorems.name: Finset.sum_image
theorems.type_signature: Set.InjOn g ↑s → ∑ x ∈ image g s, f x = ∑ x ∈ s, f (g x)
theorems.docstring:
If a function is injective on a finset, sums over the original
finset or its image coincide.
See also sum_image_of_pairwise_eq_zero for a version with weaker assumptions.

theorems.name: Finset.prod_attach
theorems.type_signature: ∏ x ∈ s.attach, f ↑x = ∏ x ∈ s, f x

theorems.name: Finset.sum_attach
theorems.type_signature: ∑ x ∈ s.attach, f ↑x = ∑ x ∈ s, f x

theorems.name: Finset.prod_congr
theorems.type_signature: (∀ x ∈ s₂, f x = g x) → s₁.prod f = s₂.prod g

theorems.name: Finset.sum_congr
theorems.type_signature: (∀ x ∈ s₂, f x = g x) → s₁.sum f = s₂.sum g

theorems.name: Finset.prod_eq_one_iff
theorems.type_signature: ∏ i ∈ s, f i = 1 ↔ ∀ i ∈ s, f i = 1
theorems.docstring: In a monoid whose only unit is 1, a product is equal to 1 iff all factors are 1.

theorems.name: Finset.sum_eq_zero_iff
theorems.type_signature: ∑ i ∈ s, f i = 0 ↔ ∀ i ∈ s, f i = 0
theorems.docstring: In an additive monoid whose only unit is 0, a sum is equal to 0 iff all terms are 0.

theorems.name: Finset.prod_disjUnion
theorems.type_signature: ∏ x ∈ s₁.disjUnion s₂ h, f x = (∏ x ∈ s₁, f x) * ∏ x ∈ s₂, f x

theorems.name: Finset.sum_disjUnion
theorems.type_signature: ∑ x ∈ s₁.disjUnion s₂ h, f x = ∑ x ∈ s₁, f x + ∑ x ∈ s₂, f x

theorems.name: Finset.prod_disjiUnion
theorems.type_signature: ∏ x ∈ s.disjiUnion t h, f x = ∏ i ∈ s, ∏ x ∈ t i, f x

theorems.name: Finset.sum_disjiUnion
theorems.type_signature: ∑ x ∈ s.disjiUnion t h, f x = ∑ i ∈ s, ∑ x ∈ t i, f x

theorems.name: Finset.prod_union_inter
theorems.type_signature: (∏ x ∈ s₁ ∪ s₂, f x) * ∏ x ∈ s₁ ∩ s₂, f x = (∏ x ∈ s₁, f x) * ∏ x ∈ s₂, f x

theorems.name: Finset.sum_union_inter
theorems.type_signature: ∑ x ∈ s₁ ∪ s₂, f x + ∑ x ∈ s₁ ∩ s₂, f x = ∑ x ∈ s₁, f x + ∑ x ∈ s₂, f x

theorems.name: Finset.prod_union
theorems.type_signature: ∏ x ∈ s₁ ∪ s₂, f x = (∏ x ∈ s₁, f x) * ∏ x ∈ s₂, f x

theorems.name: Finset.sum_union
theorems.type_signature: ∑ x ∈ s₁ ∪ s₂, f x = ∑ x ∈ s₁, f x + ∑ x ∈ s₂, f x

theorems.name: Finset.prod_filter_mul_prod_filter_not
theorems.type_signature: (∏ x ∈ s with p x, f x) * ∏ x ∈ s with ¬p x, f x = ∏ x ∈ s, f x

theorems.name: Finset.sum_filter_add_sum_filter_not
theorems.type_signature: ∑ x ∈ s with p x, f x + ∑ x ∈ s with ¬p x, f x = ∑ x ∈ s, f x

theorems.name: Finset.prod_filter_not_mul_prod_filter
theorems.type_signature: (∏ x ∈ s with ¬p x, f x) * ∏ x ∈ s with p x, f x = ∏ x ∈ s, f x

theorems.name: Finset.sum_filter_not_add_sum_filter
theorems.type_signature: ∑ x ∈ s with ¬p x, f x + ∑ x ∈ s with p x, f x = ∑ x ∈ s, f x

theorems.name: Finset.prod_filter_xor
theorems.type_signature: ∏ x ∈ s with Xor (p x) (q x), f x = (∏ x ∈ s with p x ∧ ¬q x, f x) * ∏ x ∈ s with q x ∧ ¬p x, f x

theorems.name: Finset.sum_filter_xor
theorems.type_signature: ∑ x ∈ s with Xor (p x) (q x), f x = ∑ x ∈ s with p x ∧ ¬q x, f x + ∑ x ∈ s with q x ∧ ¬p x, f x

theorems.name: IsCompl.prod_mul_prod
theorems.type_signature: (∏ i ∈ s, f i) * ∏ i ∈ t, f i = ∏ i : ι, f i

theorems.name: IsCompl.sum_add_sum
theorems.type_signature: ∑ i ∈ s, f i + ∑ i ∈ t, f i = ∑ i : ι, f i

theorems.name: Finset.prod_mul_prod_compl
theorems.type_signature: (∏ i ∈ s, f i) * ∏ i ∈ sᶜ, f i = ∏ i : ι, f i
theorems.docstring:
Multiplying the products of a function over s and over sᶜ gives the whole product.
For a version expressed with subtypes, see Fintype.prod_subtype_mul_prod_subtype.

theorems.name: Finset.sum_add_sum_compl
theorems.type_signature: ∑ i ∈ s, f i + ∑ i ∈ sᶜ, f i = ∑ i : ι, f i
theorems.docstring:
Adding the sums of a function over s and over sᶜ gives the whole sum.
For a version expressed with subtypes, see Fintype.sum_subtype_add_sum_subtype.

theorems.name: Finset.prod_compl_mul_prod
theorems.type_signature: (∏ i ∈ sᶜ, f i) * ∏ i ∈ s, f i = ∏ i : ι, f i

theorems.name: Finset.sum_compl_add_sum
theorems.type_signature: ∑ i ∈ sᶜ, f i + ∑ i ∈ s, f i = ∑ i : ι, f i

theorems.name: Finset.prod_sdiff
theorems.type_signature: (∏ x ∈ s₂ \ s₁, f x) * ∏ x ∈ s₁, f x = ∏ x ∈ s₂, f x

theorems.name: Finset.sum_sumElim
theorems.type_signature: ∑ x ∈ s.disjSum t, Sum.elim f g x = ∑ x ∈ s, f x + ∑ x ∈ t, g x

theorems.name: Finset.prod_biUnion
theorems.type_signature: ∏ x ∈ s.biUnion t, f x = ∏ x ∈ s, ∏ i ∈ t x, f i
theorems.docstring:
Given a finite family of pairwise disjoint finsets, the product over their union is the product
of the products over the sets.
See also prod_biUnion_of_pairwise_eq_one for a version with weaker assumptions.

theorems.name: Finset.sum_biUnion
theorems.type_signature: ∑ x ∈ s.biUnion t, f x = ∑ x ∈ s, ∑ i ∈ t x, f i
theorems.docstring:
Given a finite family of pairwise disjoint finsets, the sum over their union is
the sum of the sums over the sets.
See also sum_biUnion_of_pairwise_eq_zero for a version with weaker assumptions.

theorems.name: Finset.sum_fiberwise'
theorems.type_signature: ∑ j : κ, ∑ i ∈ s with g i = j, f j = ∑ i ∈ s, f (g i)

theorems.name: Finset.sum_add_distrib

theorems.type_signature: (∑ i : ι, if i ∈ s then f i else 0) = ∑ i ∈ s, f i

theorems.type_signature: ∏ a ∈ s₁ ∪ s₂, f a = ∏ a ∈ s₂, f a

theorems.type_signature: ∑ a ∈ s₁ ∪ s₂, f a = ∑ a ∈ s₂, f a

theorems.name: Finset.prod_congr_of_eq_on_inter
theorems.type_signature: ∏ a ∈ s₁, f a = ∏ a ∈ s₂, g a
theorems.docstring:
The products of two functions f g : ι → M over finite sets s₁ s₂ : Finset ι
are equal if the functions agree on s₁ ∩ s₂, f = 1 and g = 1 on the respective
set differences.

theorems.name: Finset.sum_congr_of_eq_on_inter
theorems.type_signature: ∑ a ∈ s₁, f a = ∑ a ∈ s₂, g a
theorems.docstring:
The sum of two functions f g : ι → M over finite sets s₁ s₂ : Finset ι
are equal if the functions agree on s₁ ∩ s₂, f = 0 and g = 0 on the respective
set differences.

theorems.name: Finset.prod_eq_mul_of_mem
theorems.type_signature: ∏ x ∈ s, f x = f a * f b

theorems.name: Finset.sum_eq_add_of_mem
theorems.type_signature: ∑ x ∈ s, f x = f a + f b

theorems.name: Finset.prod_eq_mul
theorems.type_signature: ∏ x ∈ s, f x = f a * f b

theorems.name: Finset.sum_eq_add
theorems.type_signature: ∑ x ∈ s, f x = f a + f b

theorems.name: Finset.prod_subtype_eq_prod_filter
theorems.type_signature: ∏ x ∈ Finset.subtype p s, f ↑x = ∏ x ∈ s with p x, f x
theorems.docstring: A product over s.subtype p equals one over {x ∈ s | p x}.

theorems.name: Finset.sum_subtype_eq_sum_filter
theorems.type_signature: ∑ x ∈ Finset.subtype p s, f ↑x = ∑ x ∈ s with p x, f x
theorems.docstring: A sum over s.subtype p equals one over {x ∈ s | p x}.

theorems.name: Finset.prod_subtype_of_mem
theorems.type_signature: ∏ x ∈ Finset.subtype p s, f ↑x = ∏ x ∈ s, f x
theorems.docstring:
If all elements of a Finset satisfy the predicate p, a product
over s.subtype p equals that product over s.

theorems.name: Finset.sum_subtype_of_mem
theorems.type_signature: ∑ x ∈ Finset.subtype p s, f ↑x = ∑ x ∈ s, f x
theorems.docstring:
If all elements of a Finset satisfy the predicate p, a sum
over s.subtype p equals that sum over s.

theorems.name: Finset.prod_subtype_map_embedding
theorems.type_signature: ∏ x ∈ map (Function.Embedding.subtype fun (x : ι) => p x) s, g x = ∏ x ∈ s, f x
theorems.docstring:
A product of a function over a Finset in a subtype equals a
product in the main type of a function that agrees with the first
function on that Finset.

theorems.name: Finset.sum_subtype_map_embedding
theorems.type_signature: ∑ x ∈ map (Function.Embedding.subtype fun (x : ι) => p x) s, g x = ∑ x ∈ s, f x
theorems.docstring:
A sum of a function over a Finset in a subtype equals a
sum in the main type of a function that agrees with the first
function on that Finset.

theorems.name: Finset.sum_coe_sort
theorems.type_signature: ∑ i : ↥s, f ↑i = ∑ i ∈ s, f i

theorems.type_signature: ∏ i : ↑↑s, f ↑i = ∏ i ∈ s, f i

theorems.name: Finset.sum_finset_coe
theorems.type_signature: ∑ i : ↑↑s, f ↑i = ∑ i ∈ s, f i

theorems.type_signature: ∏ a ∈ s, f a = ∏ a : Subtype p, f ↑a

theorems.name: Finset.sum_set_coe
theorems.type_signature: ∑ i : ↑s, f ↑i = ∑ i ∈ s.toFinset, f i

theorems.name: Finset.prod_congr_set
theorems.type_signature: ∏ i : ι, f i = ∏ i : ↑s, g i
theorems.docstring:
The product of a function g defined only on a set s is equal to
the product of a function f defined everywhere,
as long as f and g agree on s, and f = 1 off s.

theorems.name: Finset.sum_congr_set
theorems.type_signature: ∑ i : ι, f i = ∑ i : ↑s, g i
theorems.docstring:
The sum of a function g defined only on a set s is equal to
the sum of a function f defined everywhere,
as long as f and g agree on s, and f = 0 off s.

theorems.name: Finset.prod_extend_by_one

theorems.name: Finset.sum_extend_by_zero
theorems.type_signature: (∑ i ∈ s, if i ∈ s then f i else 0) = ∑ i ∈ s, f i

theorems.name: Finset.prod_eq_prod_extend
theorems.type_signature: ∏ x : ↥s, f x = ∏ x ∈ s, Function.extend Subtype.val f 1 x
theorems.docstring: Also see Finset.prod_ite_mem_eq

theorems.name: Finset.sum_eq_sum_extend
theorems.type_signature: ∑ x : ↥s, f x = ∑ x ∈ s, Function.extend Subtype.val f 0 x
theorems.docstring: Also see Finset.sum_ite_mem_eq

theorems.type_signature: ∏ x ∈ s, f x = ∏ x ∈ t, g x

theorems.name: Finset.sum_bij_ne_zero
theorems.type_signature: ∑ x ∈ s, f x = ∑ x ∈ t, g x

theorems.type_signature: ∑ x ∈ range (n + 1), f x = f n + ∑ x ∈ range n, f x

theorems.name: Finset.prod_range_succ
theorems.type_signature: ∏ x ∈ range (n + 1), f x = (∏ x ∈ range n, f x) * f n

theorems.name: Finset.sum_range_succ
theorems.type_signature: ∑ x ∈ range (n + 1), f x = ∑ x ∈ range n, f x + f n

theorems.type_signature: ∏ k ∈ range (n + 1), f k = (∏ k ∈ range n, f (k + 1)) * f 0

theorems.name: Finset.sum_range_succ'
theorems.type_signature: ∑ k ∈ range (n + 1), f k = ∑ k ∈ range n, f (k + 1) + f 0

theorems.name: Finset.sum_range_add
theorems.type_signature: ∑ x ∈ range (n + m), f x = ∑ x ∈ range n, f x + ∑ x ∈ range m, f (n + x)

theorems.type_signature: (List.map f l).sum = ∑ m ∈ l.toFinset, List.count m l • f m

theorems.type_signature: m.prod = ∏ i ∈ s, i ^ List.count i m

theorems.name: Finset.sum_list_count_of_subset
theorems.type_signature: m.sum = ∑ i ∈ s, List.count i m • i

theorems.name: Finset.prod_multiset_map_count
theorems.type_signature: (Multiset.map f s).prod = ∏ m ∈ s.toFinset, f m ^ Multiset.count m s

theorems.name: Finset.sum_multiset_map_count
theorems.type_signature: (Multiset.map f s).sum = ∑ m ∈ s.toFinset, Multiset.count m s • f m

theorems.name: Finset.prod_multiset_count
theorems.type_signature: s.prod = ∏ m ∈ s.toFinset, m ^ Multiset.count m s

theorems.name: Finset.sum_multiset_count
theorems.type_signature: s.sum = ∑ m ∈ s.toFinset, Multiset.count m s • m

theorems.name: Finset.prod_multiset_count_of_subset
theorems.type_signature: m.prod = ∏ i ∈ s, i ^ Multiset.count i m

theorems.name: Finset.sum_multiset_count_of_subset
theorems.type_signature: m.sum = ∑ i ∈ s, Multiset.count i m • i

theorems.name: Finset.prod_range_induction
theorems.type_signature: ∏ k ∈ range n, f k = s n
theorems.docstring:
For any product along {0, ..., n - 1} of a commutative-monoid-valued function, we can verify
that it's equal to a different function just by checking ratios of adjacent terms up to n.
This is a multiplicative discrete analogue of the fundamental theorem of calculus.

theorems.name: Finset.sum_range_induction
theorems.type_signature: ∑ k ∈ range n, f k = s n
theorems.docstring:
For any sum along {0, ..., n - 1} of a commutative-monoid-valued function, we
can verify that it's equal to a different function just by checking differences of adjacent terms
up to n.
This is a discrete analogue of the fundamental theorem of calculus.

theorems.name: Finset.prod_eq_pow_card
theorems.type_signature: ∏ a ∈ s, f a = b ^ s.card

theorems.name: Finset.sum_eq_card_nsmul
theorems.type_signature: ∑ a ∈ s, f a = s.card • b

theorems.name: Finset.pow_card_mul_prod
theorems.type_signature: b ^ s.card * ∏ a ∈ s, f a = ∏ a ∈ s, b * f a

theorems.name: Finset.card_nsmul_add_sum
theorems.type_signature: s.card • b + ∑ a ∈ s, f a = ∑ a ∈ s, (b + f a)

theorems.name: Finset.prod_mul_pow_card
theorems.type_signature: (∏ a ∈ s, f a) * b ^ s.card = ∏ a ∈ s, f a * b

theorems.name: Finset.sum_add_card_nsmul
theorems.type_signature: ∑ a ∈ s, f a + s.card • b = ∑ a ∈ s, (f a + b)

theorems.name: Finset.prod_pow_eq_pow_sum
theorems.type_signature: ∏ i ∈ s, a ^ f i = a ^ ∑ i ∈ s, f i

theorems.name: Finset.sum_nsmul_assoc
theorems.type_signature: ∑ i ∈ s, f i • a = (∑ i ∈ s, f i) • a

theorems.name: Finset.prod_flip
theorems.type_signature: ∏ r ∈ range (n + 1), f (n - r) = ∏ k ∈ range (n + 1), f k

theorems.name: Finset.sum_flip
theorems.type_signature: ∑ r ∈ range (n + 1), f (n - r) = ∑ k ∈ range (n + 1), f k

theorems.name: Finset.prod_involution
theorems.docstring:
The difference with Finset.prod_ninvolution is that the involution is allowed to use
membership of the domain of the product, rather than being a non-dependent function.

theorems.name: Finset.sum_involution
theorems.docstring:
The difference with Finset.sum_ninvolution is that the involution is allowed to
use membership of the domain of the sum, rather than being a non-dependent function.

theorems.name: Finset.prod_ninvolution
theorems.docstring:
The difference with Finset.prod_involution is that the involution is a non-dependent function,
rather than being allowed to use membership of the domain of the product.

theorems.name: Finset.sum_ninvolution
theorems.docstring:
The difference with Finset.sum_involution is that the involution is a
non-dependent function, rather than being allowed to use membership of the domain of the sum.

theorems.name: Finset.prod_comp
theorems.type_signature: ∏ a ∈ s, f (g a) = ∏ b ∈ image g s, f b ^ {a ∈ s | g a = b}.card
theorems.docstring:
The product of the composition of functions f and g, is the product over b ∈ s.image g of
f b to the power of the cardinality of the fibre of b. See also Finset.prod_image.

theorems.name: Finset.sum_comp
theorems.type_signature: ∑ a ∈ s, f (g a) = ∑ b ∈ image g s, {a ∈ s | g a = b}.card • f b
theorems.docstring:
The sum of the composition of functions f and g, is the sum over
b ∈ s.image g of f b times of the cardinality of the fibre of b. See also
Finset.sum_image.

theorems.name: Finset.prod_partition
theorems.type_signature: ∏ x ∈ s, f x = ∏ xbar ∈ image (Quotient.mk R) s, ∏ y ∈ s with ⟦y⟧ = xbar, f y
theorems.docstring: A product can be partitioned into a product of products, each equivalent under a setoid.

theorems.name: Finset.sum_partition
theorems.type_signature: ∑ x ∈ s, f x = ∑ xbar ∈ image (Quotient.mk R) s, ∑ y ∈ s with ⟦y⟧ = xbar, f y
theorems.docstring: A sum can be partitioned into a sum of sums, each equivalent under a setoid.

theorems.name: Finset.prod_cancels_of_partition_cancels
theorems.docstring: If we can partition a product into subsets that cancel out, then the whole product cancels.

theorems.name: Finset.sum_cancels_of_partition_cancels
theorems.docstring:
If we can partition a sum into subsets that cancel out, then the whole sum
cancels.

theorems.name: Finset.eq_of_card_le_one_of_prod_eq
theorems.docstring:
If a product of a Finset of size at most 1 has a given value, so
do the terms in that product.

theorems.name: Finset.eq_of_card_le_one_of_sum_eq
theorems.docstring:
If a sum of a Finset of size at most 1 has a given
value, so do the terms in that sum.

theorems.name: Finset.mul_prod_erase
theorems.type_signature: f a * ∏ x ∈ s.erase a, f x = ∏ x ∈ s, f x
theorems.docstring:
Taking a product over s : Finset ι is the same as multiplying the value on a single element
f a by the product of s.erase a.
See Multiset.prod_map_erase for the Multiset version.

theorems.name: Finset.add_sum_erase
theorems.type_signature: f a + ∑ x ∈ s.erase a, f x = ∑ x ∈ s, f x
theorems.docstring:
Taking a sum over s : Finset ι is the same as adding the value on a single
element f a to the sum over s.erase a.
See Multiset.sum_map_erase for the Multiset version.

theorems.name: Finset.prod_erase_mul
theorems.type_signature: (∏ x ∈ s.erase a, f x) * f a = ∏ x ∈ s, f x
theorems.docstring: A variant of Finset.mul_prod_erase with the multiplication swapped.

rather than by an inverse function.

domain of the product, rather than being a non-dependent function.

than as a surjective injection.
The difference with Finset.prod_nbij' is that the bijection and its inverse are allowed to use
membership of the domains of the products, rather than being non-dependent functions.

theorems.name: Finset.sum_bij'

theorems.name: Finset.prod_nbij

The difference with Finset.prod_bij is that the bijection is a non-dependent function, rather than

theorems.name: Finset.sum_nbij
theorems.type_signature: ∑ x ∈ s, f x = ∑ x ∈ t, g x

theorems.name: Finset.prod_nbij'
theorems.type_signature: ∏ x ∈ s, f x = ∏ x ∈ t, g x
theorems.docstring:
Reorder a product.
The difference with Finset.prod_nbij is that the bijection is specified with an inverse, rather
than as a surjective injection.
The difference with Finset.prod_bij' is that the bijection and its inverse are non-dependent
functions, rather than being allowed to use membership of the domains of the products.
The difference with Finset.prod_equiv is that bijectivity is only required to hold on the domains

The difference with Finset.sum_equiv is that bijectivity is only required to hold on the domains

theorems.name: Finset.prod_mulIndicator_subset_of_eq_one
theorems.type_signature: ∏ i ∈ t, g i ((↑s).mulIndicator f i) = ∏ i ∈ s, g i (f i)
theorems.docstring:
Consider a product of g i (f i) over a finset.  Suppose g is a function such as
n ↦ (· ^ n), which maps a second argument of 1 to 1. Then if f is replaced by the
corresponding multiplicative indicator function, the finset may be replaced by a possibly larger
finset without changing the value of the product.

theorems.name: Finset.sum_indicator_subset_of_eq_zero
theorems.type_signature: ∑ i ∈ t, g i ((↑s).indicator f i) = ∑ i ∈ s, g i (f i)
theorems.docstring:
Consider a sum of g i (f i) over a finset.  Suppose g is a function such as
n ↦ (n • ·), which maps a second argument of 0 to 0 (or a weighted sum of f i * h i or
f i • h i, where f gives the weights that are multiplied by some other function h). Then if
f is replaced by the corresponding indicator function, the finset may be replaced by a possibly
larger finset without changing the value of the sum.

taking the original function over the original finset.

theorems.name: Finset.sum_indicator_subset
theorems.type_signature: ∑ i ∈ t, (↑s).indicator f i = ∑ i ∈ s, f i
theorems.docstring:
Summing an indicator function over a possibly larger Finset is the same as
summing the original function over the original finset.

A product over all subsets of s ∪ {x} is obtained by multiplying the product over all subsets

theorems.name: List.getElem?_zero_mul_tail_prod
theorems.docstring:
We'd like to state this as L.headI * L.tail.prod = L.prod, but because L.headI relies on an
inhabited instance to return a garbage value on the empty list, this is not possible.
Instead, we write the statement in terms of L[0]?.getD 1.

theorems.name: List.getElem?_zero_add_tail_sum
theorems.docstring:
We'd like to state this as L.headI + L.tail.sum = L.sum, but because L.headI
relies on an inhabited instance to return a garbage value on the empty list, this is not possible.
Instead, we write the statement in terms of L[0]?.getD 0.

theorems.name: List.headI_add_tail_sum_of_ne_nil

theorems.docstring:

theorems.name: Finset.sum_pow_mul_eq_add_pow
theorems.type_signature: ∑ t ∈ s.powerset, a ^ t.card * b ^ (s.card - t.card) = (a + b) ^ s.card
theorems.docstring:
Summing a ^ #t * b ^ (n - #t) over all finite subsets t of a finset s
gives (a + b) ^ #s.

theorems.name: Fintype.sum_pow_mul_eq_add_pow
theorems.type_signature: ∑ s : Finset ι, a ^ s.card * b ^ (card ι - s.card) = (a + b) ^ card ι
theorems.docstring:
Summing a^#s * b^(n-#s) over all finite subsets s of a fintype of cardinality n
gives (a + b)^n. The "good" proof involves expanding along all coordinates using the fact that
x^n is multilinear, but multilinear maps are only available now over rings, so we give instead
a proof reducing to the usual binomial theorem to have a result over semirings.

theorems.name: Finset.prod_sub

theorems.docstring:
The product of f i - g i over all of s is the sum over the powerset of s of the product of
g over a subset t times the product of f over the complement of t times (-1) ^ #t.

theorems.name: Finset.prod_one_sub_ordered

a partition of unity from a collection of “bump” functions.

monoid with zero with no zero divisors, then this implication becomes an iff, see
List.prod_eq_zero_iff.

List.prod_eq_zero for an implication that needs weaker typeclass assumptions.

theorems.docstring:
Describes the counit of the adjunction M ⊗ - ⊣ Hom(M, -). Given an R-module N this
should give a map M ⊗ Hom(M, N) ⟶ N, so we flip the order of the arguments in the identity map

theorems.docstring:
Describes the unit of the adjunction M ⊗ - ⊣ Hom(M, -). Given an R-module N this should
define a map N ⟶ Hom(M, M ⊗ N), which is given by flipping the arguments in the natural
R-bilinear map M ⟶ N ⟶ M ⊗ N.
